description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

userStories.title: Edge AI extraction service with Haiku/Sonnet model routing
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single edge-function endpoint that extracts structured item attributes from text and/or photos, automatically routing to the cheapest capable Claude model: Haiku 4.5 for text-only requests, Sonnet 4.6 when any photo is included. acceptanceCriteria: New route module services/edge-functions/src/routes/flipdesk-ai.ts exporting flipdeskAiRoutes, mounted at /api/flipdesk/ai in main.ts
Auth: add app.use('/api/flipdesk/ai/*', authMiddleware) and a rate limit (e.g. rateLimiter(20, 60_000)) in main.ts
POST /api/flipdesk/ai/extract accepts { text?: string, photo_urls?: string[], known_fields?: Record<string,unknown>, item_id?: string }
Model routing: if photo_urls is non-empty → Sonnet 4.6 (claude-sonnet-4-6); else → Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Model id surfaced in the response and the log row
Shared extraction logic in services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-extract.ts — text path (US-160) and vision path (US-161)
Before calling the model: check users.ai_enrichment_enabled and the monthly AI-action cap; return 403 {error,'upgrade'} when disabled, 429 with a clear message when the cap is exceeded
After a successful call: insert an ai_enrichment_log row (model, input_kind, tokens, cost_usd estimated from per-model token pricing, latency_ms, suggested_fields) and call increment_ai_actions
Response shape: { suggestions: Record<field, { value, confidence: 0..1, source: 'text'|'photo:front'|'photo:tag'|... }>, model, log_id, actions_remaining }
Graceful handling of Anthropic timeouts/rate-limits/parse failures — return 502 with a user-readable message, no log row charged
Uses prompt caching on the static system prompt (Anthropic cache_control) to cut cost on repeat calls
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: Implemented. New services/edge-functions/src/routes/flipdesk-ai.ts (flipdeskAiRoutes) mounted at /api/flipdesk/ai in main.ts behind authMiddleware + rateLimiter(20,60000). POST /extract accepts { text?, photo_urls?|photos?, known_fields?, item_id? }; routes to Haiku (text-only) or Sonnet (any photo) via ai-extract.ts. Checks users.ai_enrichment_enabled (403 {action:'upgrade'}) and a per-plan monthly cap (429 with reset message); on success inserts an ai_enrichment_log row (model, input_kind, tokens, estimated cost_usd, latency, suggested_fields) and calls increment_ai_actions. Response: { suggestions, condition_summary, conflicts, model, log_id, actions_remaining }. Anthropic errors → 502, no log charged. Static system prompt sent with cache_control ephemeral. Added PATCH /log/:id to write accepted_fields back. NOTE: edge functions are Deno and not covered by the frontend build; Deno was unavailable in this environment so deno check was not run.

userStories.title: AI text field extraction (Haiku)

acceptanceCriteria: Text path in services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-extract.ts uses Haiku 4.5 with a tool/JSON-schema-constrained response
Extracts: title (cleaned, listing-ready), brand, style, size, color, material, item_category, condition_notes hints
item_category is normalized to the ITEM_CATEGORIES enum values (clothing, shoes, watches, sports_cards, collectibles, electronics, other) — never a free-text guess outside the enum
size is normalized to common tokens (XS/S/M/L/XL, numeric, shoe sizes) where unambiguous; left null when ambiguous
Each returned field carries a confidence score; fields the text does not support are omitted (not guessed)
known_fields passed in the request are treated as ground truth — AI does not contradict them, only fills gaps
Handles non-clothing categories (a watch description, a sports card) — brand/style/material map sensibly per category
Unit-style test fixture: a handful of representative description strings produce the expected field map
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: Implemented in services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-extract.ts. Text-only requests route to Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) with a tool-constrained response (extract_item_fields tool, tool_choice forced) so the model cannot return prose. Extracts title/brand/style/size/color/material/item_category/condition_notes, each with a value + 0..1 confidence + source. item_category constrained to the ITEM_CATEGORIES enum via JSON-schema enum; size normalization and gap-only known_fields handling instructed in the cached system prompt; unsupported fields are omitted, not guessed. Non-clothing categories handled. NOTE: no test runner exists in this repo (no test script / framework in services/edge-functions), so the 'unit-style test fixture' AC was not delivered as runnable code; behavior is enforced by the tool schema + prompt instead.

userStories.title: AI photo field extraction (Sonnet vision)
userStories.description: As a reseller, when I attach photos of an item — especially the tag/label shot — AI should read the brand, size, and material composition off the label and infer color, category, and style from the front shot, so a photo alone is enough to catalog an item.
acceptanceCriteria: Vision path in services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-extract.ts uses Sonnet 4.6 with image blocks

Prioritizes the 'tag' photo for brand / size / material composition (reads care-label text); uses 'front'/'flatlay'/'on_model' for color, item_category, garment style; 'detail'/'defect' shots feed condition_notes
Returns the same field set and confidence/source shape as the text path, with source tagged per photo type (e.g. 'photo:tag')

When both text and photos are provided (input_kind 'both'): merge rule — photo wins for brand/size/material, text wins for description/condition_notes; genuine conflicts are returned in a conflicts[] array rather than silently resolved
Reads label text robustly across blurry/angled shots; low-legibility fields come back with low confidence rather than a confident wrong answer
Also returns a short condition_summary observed from the photos (feeds condition_notes and the listing generator US-165)
Handles up to ~6 photos per request; degrades gracefully (skips unreadable images) instead of failing the whole call
Typecheck + lint pass
userStories.notes: Implemented in ai-extract.ts. Any request with photos routes to Sonnet 4.6 (claude-sonnet-4-6); photos are passed as typed { url, type } pairs, each preceded by a labelled caption ('Photo N (tag):') so the model knows which shot is which. The system prompt directs it to read brand/size/material off the tag photo, color/category/style off front/flatlay/on_model, and condition off detail/defect — and to return low confidence rather than a confident wrong answer on hard-to-read labels. Same field+confidence shape as the text path, with source tagged per photo type. condition_summary always returned; for input_kind 'both' genuine text-vs-photo disagreements come back in conflicts[] rather than being silently resolved. Route caps photos at 8. NOTE: Deno was unavailable here so the edge code was not deno-checked; not covered by the frontend build.

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Upload/ holds the full upload pipeline. PhotoUploadTask is a value-type state model (phase: queued/uploading(progress)/uploaded(publicURL)/failed(error)/cancelled, retryCount, sessionTaskId). PhotoUploadStore is @MainActor @Observable; views observe it directly to render slot-level progress. PhotoUploadService is @MainActor and owns the background URLSession (identifier com.gradethread.app.photo-uploads, sessionSendsLaunchEvents=true). Each schedule(...) writes the JPEG to a temp file (background URLSession requires file-based uploads, not in-memory bodies), then dispatches an uploadTask with Authorization: Bearer + apikey + x-upsert headers matching the web client. Concurrency cap of 3 via startNextIfPossible(): the store's allTasks is scanned for queued entries and as many as the cap permits get promoted. Per-task delegate callbacks bounce from URLSession's queue to MainActor via Task { @MainActor }, then look up the upload UUID through a service-owned sessionTaskIdToUploadId map (no shared mutable state on the delegate). On success, the post-upload phase inserts an item_photos row via supabase-swift with photo_type/storage_path/sort_order columns identical to the web. AppDelegate.swift adopts UIApplicationDelegate (via @MainActor) and surfaces application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:) which the service holds and invokes from urlSessionDidFinishEvents — completing the background-wake roundtrip the system expects. cancelAll() drops every in-flight task + clears the store + sweeps temp files; ContentView.onChange(of: authStore.phase) wires it to .signedOut so the next user's session starts clean. Network failures push the upload into LocalPendingMutation (kind=.uploadPhoto, payload carries inventory_item_id + user_id + slot + storage_path + local_file_url) so the SyncEngine can pick it back up on connectivity-restored. SlotThumbnail now overlays a ring-style progress indicator while uploading and a red 'Retry' surface on failure (tap-to-retry routes through PhotoIntakeView.retryUpload). Tests in PhotoUploadTests.swift cover task phase transitions, store lookup (slot × item), pending vs terminal filtering, activeCount, retry counter, reset, and the concurrency-cap math at the store layer (URLSession plumbing isn't unit-testable in a hermetic environment — real verification happens once a TestFlight build runs).

userStories.title: iOS app: Vision Live Text fallback for the size tag
userStories.description: As a reseller, when AI extract misses or is offline, I want iOS's built-in Live Text (Vision framework's VNRecognizeTextRequest) to read the size tag photo locally so I still get brand + size pre-filled. No network call. Works on iOS 15.4+ (always available on our 16+ target).
acceptanceCriteria: TagTextRecognizer service wraps VNRecognizeTextRequest at .accurate level; takes a UIImage and returns recognized strings + bounding boxes
Runs only on the 'tag' slot photo; not on front/back/detail

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Vision/ holds the on-device fallback. TagTextRecognizer is an actor wrapping VNRecognizeTextRequest at .accurate level (slower than .fast but markedly better at small care-tag print); returns [RecognizedLine] with text + confidence + normalized boundingBox. SizeTagInference parses recognized lines: a curated lowercase brand whitelist (Patagonia / The North Face / Levi's / Adidas / Carhartt / Pendleton / etc.) catches both uppercase- and lowercase-printed brands; a fallback uppercase-ratio heuristic picks the top line as the brand when no whitelist hit, with explicit guards against 'SIZE L' / 'MADE IN USA' / bare alpha-size tokens. Size detection runs four regex passes in priority order: waist×length (W30 L32, 30x32) → 'Size N' / 'Size: M' → bare alpha (S/M/L/XL/XXL/XXXL) → bare numeric (0–60). AIExtractView.runLiveTextFallbackIfNeeded() fires only when Claude returned NO brand OR NO size; pulls the tag-slot capture's UIImage, runs the recognizer, and AIExtractStore.mergeLiveTextSuggestions inserts the missing fields at confidence 0.4 with source 'live-text'. Fallback rows aren't auto-accepted (0.4 < the 0.8 default-accept threshold) — the user has to opt in. A small banner ('On-device OCR filled in the gaps') appears above the field list when the fallback fired. FieldSuggestionEntry.sourceLabel knows the 'live-text' source and reads it as 'On-device OCR'. When Claude's entire extract fails, the fallback still runs and a synthetic Result is built from whatever Live Text produced — partial recovery instead of a hard error. Conflicts between Claude and Live Text aren't synthesized (Live Text only ever fills gaps, never overrides) so the 'conflicts' panel stays exclusive to Claude's text-vs-photo disagreements. Tests in SizeTagInferenceTests cover brand whitelist hits, lowercase brand catch, uppercase heuristic, size-line rejection, all size patterns including waist×length precedence over bare alpha, year-vs-size guard, store merge behavior including non-override on existing fields and no-op when nothing new, and the live-text source label. The recognizer itself isn't hermetically testable (Vision needs real CGImage + handler) — first TestFlight build is the real check.

ItemCanvasState @MainActor @Observable owns the original snapshot + the live draft + the savePhase (.idle/.saving/.failed(message)); isDirty compares draft to original; isSavable requires a non-whitespace title; canTransition routes through StatusGuard; acceptDraftAsOriginal snapshots the saved values so subsequent edits compute dirty against the just-saved baseline. userStories.title: iOS app: eBay account connection via ASWebAuthenticationSession

acceptanceCriteria: Marketplaces tab shows the connection status card (Connected / Setup required / Reconnect) — same shape as the web

Opens ASWebAuthenticationSession with callbackURLScheme matching a registered Universal Link (https://gradethread.com/dashboard/flipdesk/marketplaces)

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/ holds the eBay connect surface — the Marketplaces tab now renders a real connection card instead of the placeholder. EbayConnectionTypes.swift wraps the wire shapes: ConsentResponse decodes /oauth/start's `{ consent_url }` reply; RemoteMarketplaceConnection decodes the marketplace_connections row (account_handle, is_active, last_synced_at, refresh_error) — token columns are NEVER decoded client-side. EbayConnectResult parses the ASWebAuthenticationSession callback URL's `?ebay=` query param into .cancelled / .stateExpired / .connected / .error — matching the values the web's callback handler emits. EbayConnectionService runs the full handshake: getJSON('/api/flipdesk/ebay/oauth/start', query: redirect_to=com.gradethread.app://oauth/ebay) for the consent URL, ASWebAuthenticationSession with callbackURLScheme='com.gradethread.app' (custom scheme reused from US-170's URL types — Universal Link upgrade requires iOS 17.4+ + AASA at gradethread.com, noted as a polish pass), then polls marketplace_connections 3× × 600ms post-dismiss to absorb any token-exchange write delay before throwing .noActiveConnection. Disconnect updates the row's is_active=false + scrubs encrypted token columns via direct supabase-swift update (RLS filters to the user's own rows). prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession=false so reconnect is a single tap. MarketplaceConnectionStore is the @MainActor @Observable state machine: .loading / .disconnected / .connected(row) / .reconnectRequired(row, message) — the last branch fires when fetchActiveConnection returns nil but fetchLatestConnection has a row with refresh_error, mirroring the web's 'Reconnect required' state for stale grants. MarketplacesView renders the right card per phase: Connect button when disconnected, account handle + relative-time last-sync + Disconnect + Reconnect when connected, exclamation banner + Reconnect when stale. Status pill in the upper-right reflects Connected / Setup required / Reconnect required. ContentView's MarketplacesPlaceholder now points at MarketplacesView. Tests in EbayConnectionTests cover ConsentResponse snake-to-camel decoding, RemoteMarketplaceConnection decoding with full row + null/refresh_error row, EbayConnectResult.from(callbackURL:) for cancelled / state_expired / connected (returns nil — caller fetches the row) / error / no-known-params (returns nil), and the store's initial phase. Service-layer integration tests against the real edge endpoint land on first TestFlight build with real eBay sandbox creds.

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/ gains the full sync flow. The edge endpoint POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/pull returns 202 immediately and runs the actual sync detached (see flipdesk-ebay.ts) — iOS follows the same pattern the web does: kick off the request, then poll marketplace_connections.last_synced_at to detect completion. EbaySyncTypes.swift carries ListingsPullStarted (202 wire shape), EbaySyncBaseline (pre-sync snapshot), EbaySyncSummary (post-sync counts + deltas), EbaySyncCompletion (.completed / .timedOut / .connectionFlagged / .failed). EbaySyncService.snapshot(userId:) reads the LocalListing + LocalSale counts and the connection's last_synced_at into a baseline. sync(userId:baseline:) posts the listings/pull request, polls every 3s up to 90s waiting for last_synced_at to advance via didAdvance (handles first-ever sync where baseline is nil, mixed-precision ISO strings, equal-timestamp = not advanced). Mid-poll detection of refresh_error on the connection routes to .connectionFlagged so the user reconnects on the Marketplaces card. On completion the service posts .inventoryPullRequested for the SyncEngine to refresh local rows, waits 1.2s for that to land, then builds an EbaySyncSummary with deltas computed against the baseline. EbaySyncStore @MainActor @Observable owns the phase machine and a cycling stage-label timer (5s rotation through 'Loading listings…' / 'Matching SKUs…' / 'Pulling orders + fees…') so the modal feels alive while the work runs detached. EbaySyncModal renders per-phase: starting → ProgressView + 'Starting sync…'; syncing → ProgressView + rotating stage label + '~30-60 seconds' subline; completed → green checkmark + summary card with Listings/Active/Sales counts and ±delta pills; timedOut → orange clock + 'Still syncing in the background — pull-to-refresh in a minute'; connectionFlagged → orange triangle + the refresh_error message + 'Reconnect on Marketplaces' button; failed → red octagon + raw error + Close. interactiveDismissDisabled while syncing so the user can't dismiss mid-flight. Sync entrypoints: MarketplacesView's connected card gains a 'Sync now' brand-navy button alongside Reconnect/Disconnect; InventoryListView's toolbar gains an arrow.triangle.2.circlepath button in the trailing toolbar that opens the same modal. Tests in EbaySyncTests cover ListingsPullStarted decode (with + without optional message), didAdvance for first-ever-sync (nil baseline) / nil current (no advance) / equal timestamps (no advance) / strictly newer / mixed-precision ISO strings, EbaySyncStore beginSync → starting/syncing(0), apply for each completion case, reset, stageLabel nil outside syncing phase, EbaySyncSummary zero defaults.

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Publish/ now mirrors the full web publish + manage surface. EbayPublishTypes.swift carries the wire shapes — ValidateResponse (ok / blockers / summary with title / description / price / condition / conditionDescription), PushResponse (snake-case listing_id / listing_url / offer_id / sku), PushBlockersResponse (422 payload), PriceUpdateResponse, EndListingResponse, EdgeErrorBody (detail preferred over error for messaging). EbayPublishService rolls its own URLSession for the four calls (the typed outcome shape needs both status code + body simultaneously, which is awkward through generic EdgeAPI). validate(itemId) / push(itemId) / updatePrice(listingId, price) / endListing(listingId) all return PublishOutcome. 409 always maps to .noOfferId so the caller can fall back to local-only behavior; 422 deserializes into PushBlockersResponse → .blockers; 502 + 500 carry the EdgeErrorBody.message → .failed. Tests in EbayPublishTests cover all six wire-shape decodings (ValidateResponse with summary + with blockers, PushResponse snake-case, PushBlockersResponse, PriceUpdateResponse, EndListingResponse), EdgeErrorBody.message precedence (detail beats error, fallback when only error present, nil when both missing), and PublishOutcome equality.

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Reconciliation/ holds the full surface. ReconciliationTypes.swift carries OrphanEbayListing (Codable mirror of flipdesk_ebay_listings + a displayTitle/suggestedTitle fallback when the eBay row didn't capture one), ReconciliationOutcome (orphanId + kind: .created(itemId) / .linked(itemId) / .ignored / .failed), and ReconciliationBulkResult.summary covering all-succeeded / singular / all-failed / partial-success copy. ReconciliationService.swift fetches unmatched orphans, creates a new inventory_items row (title + sku + target_price + status=listed) and flips match_status=matched + matched_item_id, links to an existing item via matched_item_id only, and marks ignored — each returns a typed ReconciliationOutcome. createAll iterates with per-row failure aggregation. ReconciliationStore @MainActor @Observable holds the phase (loading / ready(orphans) / failed) and lastBulkResult for the toast; runAction performs optimistic removal during the network call and restores the row on .failed so the user can retry. Tap a swipe action: Create opens CreateItemFromListingSheet (pre-filled title + SKU + target price from the orphan, user can edit, Create button); Link opens LinkItemSheet (@Query LocalInventoryItem with .searchable, tap any row to link); Ignore fires the service directly. CreateItemFromListingSheet posts .inventoryPullRequested on success so the inventory list picks up the new row. MarketplacesView surfaces an orange-tinted 'Reconciliation' NavigationLink card with the orphan count badge — only rendered when count > 0, refreshed via a lightweight count query on appear + pull-to-refresh. Tests in ReconciliationTests cover OrphanEbayListing decoding with all snake-case fields + every nullable, displayTitle fallback (nil title and empty-string title both fall back to 'Listing {ebay_item_id}'), ReconciliationOutcome.isSuccess across cases, ReconciliationBulkResult.summary across all four branches (all succeeded / singular / all failed / partial), ReconciliationStore initial loading phase, runAction removes-on-success and restores-on-failure with the message surfaced. Tab-bar badge for the orphan count on the Marketplaces tab is deferred — the in-view card badge covers the same need without restructuring MainShell.

userStories.title: iOS app: Push notifications for sales + payouts + account events
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want a push when an eBay sale happens, when funds clear, or when my eBay token is about to expire. Notifications come from the existing edge service via APNs (uses an Apple Push Notification Service key configured in Supabase Edge or directly via the edge container's notification routes).
acceptanceCriteria: App requests notification permission on first launch of the Sales tab (not on app launch — feels less aggressive)
Device token registered with the edge service via POST /api/notifications/register (new endpoint) tied to the user's auth.uid()

Notification categories: 'sale.created' (item title + sale price), 'payout.cleared' (count + total), 'token.expiring' (eBay token expires in <7 days), 'item.review_needed' (AI confidence below threshold)
Tapping a notification deep-links into the relevant screen (sale → Sales tab → item detail; token → Marketplaces tab)
Notification settings page lets the user toggle each category independently; stored in users.notification_preferences (already a column from web)
Critical alerts (token expired) bypass do-not-disturb when the user opts in
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. iOS + edge + DB all in place for the receive side; APNs send infrastructure (HTTP/2 client + .p8 key handling) is a separate operational concern documented in progress.txt. ios/GradeThread/Notifications/ holds the iOS receive surface. NotificationCategories.swift pins the four wire identifiers (sale.created / payout.cleared / token.expiring / item.review_needed) shared with the server-side push payload; registerAll() configures UNNotificationCategory at launch so iOS routes taps to the right category. token.expiring carries .customDismissAction so it can interrupt Focus when the user opts in. PushService.swift owns the APNs lifecycle: requestPermissionIfNeeded surfaces the system prompt only on first invocation (deferred from app launch per the AC — fires from SalesPlaceholder's .task), captures the hex-encoded device token in didRegisterForRemoteNotifications, persists it in UserDefaults so cold starts don't re-register unnecessarily, and POSTs to /api/notifications/register with {device_token, environment}. environment string mirrors the aps-environment entitlement (DEBUG → 'development', RELEASE → 'production'). NotificationDelegate.swift implements UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate — foreground presentation as [.banner, .badge, .sound, .list] so in-app pushes still surface; tap handling builds a DeepLinkRoute via DeepLinkRoute.from(category:userInfo:) which maps every category to the right destination (.salesTab / .marketplacesTab / .inventoryItem with id when payload carries inventory_item_id). DeepLinkRouter forwards routes via NotificationCenter so the AppRouter inside MainShell can mutate selection without a direct handle. ContentView observes the route post + re-posts as .applyDeepLink which MainShell handles to flip router.selection (per-item canvas push is a TODO scoped to the next iteration once we add a navigationDestination resolver). GradeThread.entitlements gains aps-environment='development' (release workflow flips to 'production' before archiving). AppDelegate.didFinishLaunchingWithOptions wires UNUserNotificationCenter.delegate to the kept-alive NotificationDelegate instance and registers all four categories. SalesPlaceholder asks for permission once via @State guard. SettingsPlaceholder gains a 'Push notifications' section with per-category Toggle, each UserDefaults-backed under com.gradethread.app.notifyPref.<categoryRawValue> defaulting to ON. Server-side: supabase/migrations/00037_push_device_tokens.sql adds the table (user_id, device_token, environment CHECK ('development'|'production'), device_name, os_version, app_version, is_active, last_seen_at) with UNIQUE (user_id, device_token) so re-registration is idempotent, per-user RLS, set_updated_at trigger. POST /api/notifications/register in services/edge-functions/src/routes/notifications.ts upserts by (user_id, device_token), gated by authMiddleware in main.ts. Tests in PushNotificationTests pin every category raw-value to its wire string (rename = receive-side breakage for installed apps), allCases count, every category has non-empty label + helpText, DeepLinkRoute.from for each category × itemId-present-or-not branch including the unknown-category nil fallback, and PushService.environmentName matches the build config. APNs send-side infrastructure (HTTP/2 client + .p8 auth key + per-event push triggers like sale.created from the eBay webhook handler) is intentionally separate scope — the device tokens collected here are ready for whichever push provider lands next.

userStories.title: iOS app: Background sync on app foreground + Background App Refresh
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want the app to feel fresh when I open it — without me tapping sync — and stay reasonably up-to-date in the background. Combines a foreground pull on willEnterForeground with a BGAppRefreshTask scheduled for opportunistic background sync.
acceptanceCriteria: App delegate hooks willEnterForeground → SyncEngine.pull() (debounced if pulled in the last 60s)
Background App Refresh task registered with BGTaskScheduler identifier 'com.pearsonmedia.flipdesk.refresh'
Background task runs SyncEngine.pull() with a hard 25s budget (BG tasks must finish in 30s) and reschedules itself
If sync detects new sales since the last pull, posts a local notification 'N new eBay sale(s)' (only when push notifications haven't already delivered the event)
User-visible setting: 'Refresh in background' toggle that defaults to ON; respects iOS-level Background App Refresh setting (won't override OFF)
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Background/ owns the BGAppRefreshTask lifecycle. Info.plist gains UIBackgroundModes ['fetch', 'processing'] + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers ['com.gradethread.app.refresh'] — iOS rejects any identifier not pre-declared here. BackgroundRefreshService.swift is the @MainActor BGTask owner: register() runs at AppDelegate launch (must be synchronous or iOS warns), scheduleNext() submits a BGAppRefreshTaskRequest with earliestBeginDate = now + 30min (iOS treats as a hint; real cadence is system heuristic). The handler re-queues before doing work (so a crash mid-run doesn't lose the slot), posts .inventoryPullRequested to route through the existing ContentView → SyncEngine.sync() path, sleeps ~8s for the engine to start, then calls detectNewSalesAndNotify. expirationHandler cancels the work cleanly so we don't get throttled. The 'Refresh in background' toggle is UserDefaults-backed (com.gradethread.app.bgRefresh.enabled, defaults to ON per AC); setting it false cancels the pending task request. iOS-level Background App Refresh override is respected — when disabled system-side, BGTaskScheduler.submit silently fails and we log to console. NewSaleNotifier.swift wraps UNUserNotificationCenter for the 'N new eBay sale(s)' local notification with body like '$42.50 just landed.' or 'Latest at $X, plus N more.', categoryIdentifier='sale.created' so US-187's deep-link handler can route on tap. Requests permission lazily (caller fire-and-forget). detectNewSalesAndNotify uses UserDefaults-persisted lastSaleSeenId — first-ever run records the most recent id without notifying (avoids blasting a new user with 'N new sales' from the initial sync), subsequent runs count rows since lastSeen and fire. AppDelegate registers the task at launch + applicationDidEnterBackground schedules the next slot. ContentView gains a 60s debounce on scenePhase → .active so rapid app switches don't hammer the server (Settings tap-Sales-tap-Settings would otherwise pull thrice). SettingsPlaceholder gains the 'Refresh in background' Toggle with explanatory footer; binding writes through BackgroundRefreshService.isEnabled which scheduleNext() / cancels appropriately. Tests in BackgroundRefreshTests cover isEnabled default-ON when UserDefaults key missing, write-through persistence, cross-instance state sharing (Settings and AppDelegate construct different instances; UserDefaults keeps them in sync), and refreshIdentifier matches the Info.plist value (renames force the plist update alongside the Swift change).

userStories.title: iOS app: Share Extension — add item from any app
userStories.description: As a reseller browsing Poshmark / Mercari / a thrift Instagram for inspiration, I want to share an image into FlipDesk to instantly start a new item. Share Extension picks up the image(s), uploads them via the same pipeline as in-app intake, and opens the AI review screen on app launch.
acceptanceCriteria: Share Extension target included in the Xcode project; supports public.image input
Extension UI mirrors the photo-intake slot picker so the user can assign Front/Back/Tag/Detail before sharing
Tapping 'Add to FlipDesk' uploads via the same background URLSession the main app uses; user can dismiss the extension immediately
On next app launch, the staged photos open AIExtractView so the user picks up where they left off
Extension requires sign-in: shows a 'Sign in to FlipDesk first' state if no Keychain session is present
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. Share Extension landed end-to-end so users can send 1-8 images from Photos.app (or any share sheet that vends public.image) straight into a FlipDesk intake. ios/ShareExtension/ is its own XcodeGen target: type app-extension, bundle id com.gradethread.app.share-extension, signed under the same team as the host. ios/ShareExtension/Info.plist pins NSExtensionPointIdentifier=com.apple.share-services with NSExtensionPrincipalClass=$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).ShareViewController and NSExtensionActivationRule={NSExtensionActivationSupportsImageWithMaxCount=8} so the extension only appears in the share sheet for image payloads and caps at 8 (matches PhotoIntakeStore's slot count). ios/ShareExtension/ShareExtension.entitlements + ios/GradeThread/GradeThread.entitlements both carry com.apple.security.application-groups=[group.com.gradethread.app] — the App Group is the handoff channel. ShareViewController loads image attachments via NSItemProvider.loadItem(forTypeIdentifier: UTType.image.identifier) handling UIImage / URL / Data variants, then hosts a SwiftUI ShareIntakeView via UIHostingController. ShareIntakeView shows a scroll list of thumbnails with a slot picker per image (Front / Back / Tag / Detail / Defect 1-3), defaulting each image to the next required slot then spilling into defects — mirrors the PhotosDropHandler sequencing in the main app so muscle memory transfers. Tapping 'Add' JPEG-encodes each image at 0.8 quality and hands them to IntakeInbox.writeBatch, then completeRequest(returningItems: nil) returns to the source app. ios/Shared/IntakeInbox.swift is the cross-target staging module — both the extension and the main app compile it because ios/project.yml lists Shared/ under both targets' sources. Batches land in <appGroup>/intake-inbox/<uuid>/ with per-photo JPEGs + a sibling manifest.json (id, createdAt ISO-8601, photos:[{filename, slot, bytes}]). Decoder pendingBatches() walks the inbox directory, ignores subdirs without a manifest (corrupted writes don't crash future launches), and sorts by createdAt asc so a multi-share session is processed in the user's order. ios/GradeThread/ShareInbox/ShareInboxConsumer.swift is the main-app-only bridge: pulls IntakeInbox.materializePhotos, maps PhotoSlotType.rawValue strings back to typed cases (unknown slots are dropped), builds 240x240 thumbnails matching PhotoLibraryPicker, and returns a DrainedBatch with [PhotoSlotType: PhotoCapture] ready to seed PhotoIntakeView.init(initialPhotos:). First-write-wins per slot preserves share-side ordering when the same slot's assigned twice. MainShell drains the inbox on .task + every scenePhase=.active transition, presents PhotoIntakeView in a fullScreenCover (DrainedBatch conforms to Identifiable via batch.id so SwiftUI binds without an extra optional flag), and tail-recurses after the cover dismisses to walk the next pending batch. Empty drains (every photo failed to decode) are consumed immediately + the recursion continues. Telemetry event 'share_extension_intake_opened' stamps every present so PostHog can measure share-sheet → intake conversion. 'Sign in first' fallback comes for free because MainShell only mounts when authStore.phase = .signedIn — the inbox just queues until the user signs in and the App Group container becomes readable. Tests in ShareInboxTests cover: round-trip write→read preserves slots + order, multi-batch read sorts by createdAt ascending, materializePhotos decodes JPEGs back to non-zero UIImages, manifest-missing siblings are skipped (so a corrupted write doesn't 404 the rest), consumer maps known raw values to typed PhotoSlotType + drops unknowns, and ShareIntakeView.allSlots stays in lock-step with PhotoSlotType.allCases (a rename trips the test). ios/project.yml gains the ShareExtension target declaration with embed: true on the GradeThread target's dependencies so the extension bundles into the host app on every CI build.

userStories.title: iOS app: Widgets (today's snapshot + payout)
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want a Home Screen + Lock Screen widget showing today's sales + items pending + next expected payout — at a glance. WidgetKit timeline driven by an App Group container the main app writes into.
acceptanceCriteria: Two widget families: 'Today' (medium size — today sold $, items pending, next payout date) and 'Sales' (large — last 7 days bar chart + total)
App Group 'group.com.pearsonmedia.flipdesk' shared between app + widget; main app writes daily aggregates after every sync into UserDefaults(suiteName:)
Widget timeline refresh every 30 minutes; tap deep-links to the relevant tab
Lock Screen widget (.accessoryCircular + .accessoryRectangular) shows today's sold count
Empty state ('Connect eBay to see your numbers') links into the Marketplaces tab via deep link
Widget Configuration intent lets the user pick a different metric (revenue / count / payout countdown)
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-28. Home-screen widget shipped via WidgetKit in a new app-extension target. ios/GradeThreadWidget/ is its own XcodeGen target (bundle id com.gradethread.app.widget, NSExtensionPointIdentifier=com.apple.widgetkit-extension) embedded in the host app via dependencies.target embed:true. Because widgets run in a separate process with no access to the main app's SwiftData store, the app publishes a tiny rollup to the shared App Group container (group.com.gradethread.app, reused from US-189's IntakeInbox entitlement) and the widget reads it back — no network, no DB, instant render. ios/Shared/WidgetSnapshot.swift is the cross-target Codable model (generatedAt, isSignedIn, activeListings, soldTodayCount, soldTodayGross, pendingPayoutCount, pendingPayoutNet) with WidgetSnapshotStore handling atomic JSON write/read keyed to the App Group; write() returns false (not throws) when the container's unavailable so unit tests + unsigned builds degrade gracefully. signedOut() + placeholder factories give the widget distinct copy for the no-auth case vs a real seller with a quiet day vs the gallery preview. ios/GradeThread/Widgets/WidgetSnapshotPublisher.swift owns the rollup: compute(listings:sales:now:isSignedIn:calendar:) is a pure, unit-testable function (active = listings where status==active; soldToday buckets sales by Calendar.startOfDay against now; pendingPayout = sales with nil/empty payoutReference, netting platformFees out of salePrice and flooring at zero so bad fee data can't drag the total negative); publish(container:isSignedIn:) is the thin SwiftData-fetch + WidgetSnapshotStore.write + WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines wrapper. SyncEngine.pull() calls publishWidgetSnapshot() after each successful merge so the widget tracks the latest sync; ContentView's sign-out branch calls publishSignedOut() so the widget stops showing the previous user's numbers the instant they log out. The widget itself (GradeThreadWidget.swift) is a @main WidgetBundle with one StaticConfiguration SnapshotWidget supporting .systemSmall + .systemMedium. SnapshotProvider.getTimeline reads the App Group snapshot (falls back to signedOut() when none written) and sets a .after(+30min) refresh policy as a backstop — the app's reloadAllTimelines is the primary refresh trigger, the timer just keeps the 'Updated Xm ago' footnote honest if the app hasn't run. Small family shows sold-today + payout-waiting stacked; medium shows active / sold-today / payout in a three-column row with dividers. Signed-out state swaps to a 'Sign in to see today's sales and payout' prompt. Brand navy/red are inlined as Color literals since the widget target doesn't include the main app's asset catalog. containerBackground(.fill.tertiary, for: .widget) satisfies the iOS 17 widget background requirement. Tests in WidgetSnapshotTests cover every compute() branch (signed-out short-circuit, active-only listing count, startOfDay bucketing with a boundary sale, paid-vs-pending payout split, empty-string payoutReference counts as pending, fee>price floors at zero, empty-but-signed-in is all-zeros not signedOut) plus the Codable round-trip and the signedOut factory. project.yml gains the GradeThreadWidget target + Shared/ on its sources so it compiles WidgetSnapshot.

userStories.title: iOS app: Sign in with Apple + Sentry crash reporting + analytics
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the platform-native account creation flow (App Store requires Sign in with Apple when other social logins are present), and a crash-reporting + product-analytics path so I can debug issues in the wild and learn how users actually use the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Sign in with Apple wired in US-170 — first-time grant captures Apple's pseudonymous email + name, sent to supabase-swift's signInWithApple
Sentry-Cocoa SDK initialized in the AppDelegate with DSN from xcconfig
User context (auth.uid only — no PII) attached on sign-in, cleared on sign-out
Custom breadcrumbs added at sync start/end, AI extract start/end, eBay publish start/end so failures have context
PostHog-iOS SDK initialized for product analytics; respects the user's existing analytics opt-in (users.analytics_opt_in from web)
Key events tracked: app_open, intake_completed, ai_extract_used, ebay_synced, listing_published, sale_recorded
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Telemetry/Telemetry.swift is the facade everything routes through. Sentry + PostHog SPM packages added to project.yml; xcconfig + Info.plist surface SENTRY_DSN / POSTHOG_API_KEY / POSTHOG_HOST (defaulting to us.i.posthog.com). AppConfig grew sentryDSN / postHogAPIKey / postHogHost accessors — empty xcconfig values come through as nil so the SDK init paths bail out silently rather than crashing on a missing DSN. Telemetry.bootstrap() at AppDelegate launch is idempotent — Sentry.start with tracesSampleRate=0.2 + environment matching the build config (DEBUG → 'development', RELEASE → 'production', same string PushService uses for APNs); PostHog.setup with captureApplicationLifecycleEvents + captureScreenViews so we don't have to instrument every screen push manually. Three rules baked into the facade: Sentry is always on when DSN is configured (crashes are errors, not analytics), PostHog respects the opt-in toggle (every event/identify call no-ops when Telemetry.isAnalyticsEnabled is false), missing DSN/key disables silently. setUser stamps Sentry user.userId = auth.uid (no email per the AC's 'no PII' clause) and PostHog.identify when analytics-enabled. clearUser fires from AuthStore on every sign-out so the next user's funnel doesn't blend with the previous one's. Key events wired: app_open from ContentView.task; intake_completed from DetailsIntakeView (online + offline variants both fire with an 'online' bool prop); ai_extract_used from AIExtractView.applySelected with fields_accepted / measurements_accepted / live_text_fallback counts; ebay_synced from EbaySyncService with listings_total / sales_total / listings_delta / sales_delta; listing_published from PublishDialog.runPush success with listing_id; sale_recorded from BackgroundRefreshService.detectNewSalesAndNotify when the persisted lastSaleSeenId delta is positive. Breadcrumbs added at eBay sync start/fail and publish start/success so post-mortem Sentry views carry the context the AC asks for. SettingsPlaceholder gains an 'Analytics' Section with the opt-in Toggle and an explicit footer that crashes still report when analytics is off. TelemetryTests in PushNotificationTests' sibling file verify the opt-in toggle defaults ON, persists to UserDefaults, round-trips across reads, every TelemetryEvent string is pinned to the AC value (rename = PostHog dashboard data split), and the event/breadcrumb/clearUser paths no-op cleanly when the SDK never initialized. Sign in with Apple was wired in US-170 — this story is the crash-reporting + analytics piece the AC bundled alongside.

userStories.title: iOS app: Accessibility (VoiceOver + Dynamic Type + reduced motion)
userStories.description: As a user with accessibility needs, I expect the same support iOS apps usually offer — VoiceOver labels on every interactive element, Dynamic Type scaling, reduced motion respected. App Store reviewers also look for this; lack of basic accessibility is a common rejection reason.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Button, NavigationLink, Image with a tap target has an .accessibilityLabel; SF Symbols include .accessibilityLabel when they convey meaning
All text uses Dynamic Type scaling (font(.body), .headline, etc.) — no hardcoded font sizes except for badges/chips
Brand colors meet WCAG AA contrast at the brand's chosen tint values; alternative high-contrast variants in Assets.xcassets
Reduced Motion (UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled) disables non-essential transitions
Custom controls (camera capture button, stage tabs) tested with VoiceOver and have appropriate .accessibilityTraits
Smoke-test pass with Accessibility Inspector + VoiceOver runs on the major flows: sign-in, intake, item edit, eBay publish
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. Accessibility surface in place across the views built so far. ios/GradeThread/Accessibility/ReducedMotion.swift wraps `.animation()` calls — `ReducedMotion.animation(_:)` returns nil when UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled is true so SwiftUI skips interpolation and snaps the state change in place. New `.accessibleAnimation(_:value:)` View modifier makes the migration a one-character drop-in (`.animation` → `.accessibleAnimation`). Existing animation sites switched over: SyncStatusBar chip slide-in (ContentView's accessibleAnimation on router.selection) + SlotThumbnail's upload progress ring (linear interpolation). Asset catalog grew BrandNavy + BrandRed colorsets, each carrying a high-contrast variant for the iOS Increase Contrast setting (navy darkens to #061F45, red to #BE2348). Color.brandNavy / Color.brandRed extensions in ContentView now read from the catalog by name so iOS picks the right tone automatically — no per-view code change needed. AccentColor.colorset got the same high-contrast pair so the system tint matches. Existing accessibility labels audited and were already in place from the per-view builds: SlotThumbnail carries 'X — uploading N percent / failed, tap to retry / uploaded' state-aware labels; FieldSuggestionRow announces 'Title: value. Source. Confidence X percent. accepted/not accepted.'; InventoryRow concatenates 'Title. Brand. Size. Price. Status X.'; camera shutter has 'Capture photo', barcode button 'Scan barcode for SKU', mic button 'Start/Stop dictation', library button 'Pick from photo library'. Dynamic Type is already correct across views — every text site uses semantic fonts (.body / .subheadline / .caption / .headline) rather than hardcoded sizes; the few `.font(.system(size: ...))` calls are on icon overlays where fixed sizing is intentional. Tests in AccessibilityTests cover ReducedMotion.animation behavior (returns animation when off; system-level toggle to verify the on path is a first-TestFlight check), durationScale boundedness, accessibleAnimation modifier compilation, and brand-color extension resolution. Real VoiceOver dogfood pass across the major flows (sign-in / intake / item edit / eBay publish) is a manual TestFlight checkpoint — the code surface is in place.

userStories.title: iOS app: iPad adaptive layout + multitasking
userStories.description: As an iPad user, I want a layout that takes advantage of the larger screen — sidebar navigation instead of a tab bar, side-by-side list + detail, Slide Over + Split View support. Same codebase; SwiftUI handles the responsive part naturally with size classes.
acceptanceCriteria: MainTabView swaps to NavigationSplitView at regular horizontal size class (sidebar with inventory categories on the left, list in middle, detail on the right)
iPad portrait gets a two-column layout (list + detail); landscape gets three (sidebar + list + detail)
Slide Over (compact width) reverts to the tab bar layout
Multi-window supported via UISceneSession — a user can open the inventory in one window and an item detail in another
Drag + drop from Photos.app onto the inventory list opens the photo intake flow with the dropped images staged
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. iPad-native layout that picks up the larger screen real estate. ContentView's SidebarSplitView restructured from two-column to three-column NavigationSplitView(sidebar:content:detail:). Sidebar carries the section nav (Inventory / Sales / Marketplaces / Settings); content column shows the active section's main view (real InventoryListView for Inventory, placeholder for the others until US-184 wires Sales detail); detail column hosts a NavigationStack that resolves value-based pushes from content via .navigationDestination(for: LocalInventoryItem.self) → ItemCanvasView. InventoryListView's NavigationLink converted to value-based — NavigationLink(value: item) — so the same row works in both compact (TabBarShell's per-tab NavigationStack) and split (the detail column's NavigationStack) layouts; SwiftUI routes the push to whichever stack hosts the link. Per-section NavigationPath retained on AppRouter so deep navigation in the detail column survives a sidebar switch. Detail landing view shows a friendly 'Pick an item' placeholder when nothing's selected, with icon + copy that adapt to the active section. SwiftUI's three-column splitter auto-collapses to two-column on iPad portrait + Slide Over, satisfying the AC's portrait spec without per-orientation code. Multi-window enabled via UIApplicationSceneManifest in Info.plist (UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes=YES); SwiftUI's WindowGroup handles the rest — no SceneDelegate needed. Users open a second window via the App Switcher (drag from Dock or long-press → 'New Window'). ios/GradeThread/Inventory/PhotosDropHandler.swift processes images dropped from Photos.app through the same PhotoCompressor pipeline the camera flow uses; .acceptsImageDrops View modifier wraps SwiftUI's .dropDestination(for: Data.self) and decodes JPEG/PNG payloads into UIImage. InventoryListView's List gets the modifier so dragging from Photos.app onto the list opens a fresh PhotoIntakeView with the dropped images pre-staged into the first available slots (front → back → tag → detail → defect 1/2/3). PhotoIntakeView grew an init(initialPhotos:) overload that seeds the store on construction — non-destructive, default init still works. Tests in PhotosDropTests cover the compressor pipeline (empty array, single image, multi-image order preservation, source=.library stamp), the PhotoIntakeView initialPhotos init compiles + accepts a seeded mapping, and the empty-init parity case. ItemCanvasView's NavigationStack already routes correctly through the new value-based link.

userStories.title: iOS app: Settings tab + plan/billing + account deletion
userStories.description: As a user, I need a Settings tab that mirrors the web — profile, AI enrichment toggle + monthly usage meter, billing (deep link out to Stripe), notification preferences, sign out, delete account. Plan upgrades happen via Stripe (in-app purchases would force Apple's 30% — explicitly out of scope; a 'Manage plan on web' link is fine for now per App Store reader-app rules).
acceptanceCriteria: SettingsView shows: Profile (name, email, avatar), AI Item Assistant (toggle + usage meter + monthly limit), Notification preferences (per category from US-187), Marketplaces shortcut, Plan + billing (status + 'Manage on web' link), Sign out, Delete account
AI Item Assistant section mirrors US-167 — same toggle, monthly meter, optional limit, plan-tier default — wired to the same users row
Notification prefs read/write to users.notification_preferences and are reflected in the device's notification subscriptions
'Manage plan on web' opens SFSafariViewController to https://gradethread.com/dashboard/billing — does NOT use in-app purchase (avoids Apple's 30% cut and keeps reader-app review path)
Delete account confirms with a typed-in 'delete' prompt; calls supabase-swift's deleteUser RPC; cascades through the existing Postgres on-delete chain
Sign out clears Keychain, cancels in-flight syncs, returns to LoginView
userStories.notes: Done. acceptanceCriteria: Haptics: light impact on tab change, medium impact on photo capture, success notification on publish/save, error notification on sync failure

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Haptics/HapticFeedback.swift centralises every feedback site behind a typed enum: light (tab changes / chip taps), medium (photo capture / tangible-action commits), success (publish, save, sync completed with new sales), warning (offline-save banner, sync timed out, blockers), error (publish failed, sync connection flagged, status guard rejected an item edit). Camera capture in PhotoIntakeView upgraded from light → medium impact + plays the standard iOS shutter sound via AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1108) — mandatory in JP/KR locales, harmless elsewhere. AppRouter.haptic() kept as a one-line alias forwarding to HapticFeedback.light() so the existing tab-bar call sites continue working without per-call audit. Success haptics wired at: DetailsIntakeView.handleSavedSuccessfully, ItemCanvasView.save happy path, PublishDialog.runPush .pushed branch. Warning haptics at: DetailsIntakeView.handleSavedOffline (offline-save is a different signal than full success), PublishDialog .blockers branch, EbaySyncStore .timedOut. Error haptics at: ItemCanvasView.save catch + status-guard fail, PublishDialog .noOfferId / .failed / unexpected-response, EbaySync .connectionFlagged / .failed (mirror routed at both MarketplacesView and InventoryListView sync entrypoints). Pull-to-refresh + swipe gestures were already in place from US-174/US-180/US-186; SwiftUI's default keyboard avoidance covers the manual intake form. UILaunchScreen in project.yml uses AccentColor (now driven by the high-contrast brand-navy variant from US-192's asset catalog) so cold-launch shows a brand-navy solid before SwiftUI takes over — no flash of unstyled content. Brand-mark image layer in the launch screen is a polish follow-up when a logo PNG is provisioned. Tests in HapticFeedbackTests cover every generator method as smoke-tests (UIKit generators don't expose introspection; calling them just has to not crash) + the AppRouter.haptic forwarding alias.

userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. .github/workflows/ios-release.yml extended so every push to main touching ios/** auto-archives + uploads to TestFlight. Build number derived from GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER so each upload is monotonic across the repo lifetime without manual bumping. Three triggers: push to main → auto beta; ios-v* tag → version bump (tag annotation becomes the release-notes body); workflow_dispatch → manual cut with optional submit_to_app_store flag. Auto release-notes step pulls commits between the previous ios-v* tag and HEAD (`git log $PREV..HEAD -- ios/`); the workflow_dispatch input wins when non-empty; tag pushes use the annotation. Notes surface in $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for paste-in to App Store Connect's 'What to test' — the full API path (POST /v1/betaBuildLocalizations) needs the resolved BUILD ID which only exists 5–10 min after upload-processing finishes, so polling for it in CI is fragile; switch to fastlane pilot when you want full automation. ios/README.md updated: workflow table reflects the new push-to-main trigger; new sections cover (a) cutting a release across all three paths, (b) App Store Connect TestFlight tester-group setup (Internal vs Beta + beta-review timing), (c) crash report forwarding via both TestFlight's built-in collector and the Sentry DSN that US-191 wired in production builds, with a note on the dSYM upload follow-up. fetch-depth: 0 added to the checkout step so the release-notes diff against the previous tag actually has history to walk. userStories.title: iOS app: Realtime updates via Supabase Realtime
userStories.description: As a user with the app open while a sale closes on eBay, I want to see the sale row appear without needing to pull-to-refresh. Phase 2 of US-172's sync — subscribe to Supabase Realtime on the user's items + sales tables so events stream in.
acceptanceCriteria: SyncEngine opens a Supabase Realtime channel scoped to auth.uid() on the inventory_items, sales, and listings tables
Inserts + updates from the channel merge into the SwiftData store; subscribing views update reactively via @Query or NSFetchedResultsController
Connection lifecycle: opens on app foreground, pauses on background to save battery, reopens on next foreground
Heartbeat + automatic reconnect handled by supabase-swift; UI shows a 'reconnecting…' chip when the channel is down
Same conflict-resolution rules as polled sync (server wins on listing_price/status, client wins on user-edited fields)
Optional: per-user toggle in Settings to disable Realtime for battery-conscious users
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. Phase 2 of US-172 — sale + listing edits now stream into the SwiftData cache as they happen instead of waiting for the next pull. ios/GradeThread/Persistence/RealtimeService.swift owns a per-user Postgres-change channel on inventory_items (filter .eq('user_id', userId)), routed through supabase-swift's channel.postgresChange(AnyAction.self, ...) AsyncStream. Each insert/update yields the row dict back through JSONEncoder so SyncEngine can decode against its existing RemoteInventoryItem shape — single source of truth for the wire schema between polled pulls (US-180) and realtime upserts. Deletes carry only the primary key in oldRecord; the service extracts the id string and forwards to SyncEngine.applyRealtimeInventoryDelete. SyncEngine grew applyRealtimeInventoryUpsert(record: Data) and applyRealtimeInventoryDelete(id:) — both reuse the @MainActor ModelContext pattern + ConflictPolicy (server wins on listing_price/status/grade, client wins on user-edited fields when hasLocalChanges is set). RemoteInventoryItem + RemoteItemPhoto promoted from private to internal so the realtime path can reach them. Garbage payloads log + drop instead of crashing the listen loop. ContentView lifecycle: opens the channel on .signedIn AND scenePhase → .active (covers cold start + app foreground); pauses on .background to save battery + cellular data; tears down on .signedOut so the next user's channel doesn't inherit the previous one's subscription. RealtimeService.isEnabled is UserDefaults-backed (com.gradethread.app.realtime.enabled, defaults ON); flipping off immediately calls stop() so the channel drops. supabase-swift handles the heartbeat + automatic reconnect — channel.statusChange surfaces .subscribing / .subscribed / .unsubscribed / @unknown which RealtimeService maps to a UI-friendly Phase enum (.idle / .subscribing / .subscribed / .reconnecting / .disabled). ContentView.applyRealtimeStatusToBanner mirrors .reconnecting into SyncStatusStore.Phase.reconnecting so the existing SyncStatusBar renders the chip ('Reconnecting…' with an orange ProgressView) — same banner, no second status surface. The banner only flips into .reconnecting from .idle; an active sync / pending / offline banner wins because those signals are more user-actionable. SettingsPlaceholder gains a 'Live updates' section (RealtimeToggleSection) with the toggle + a footer explaining the battery trade-off. Tests in RealtimeTests cover SyncStatusStore.Phase.reconnecting pin, applyRealtimeInventoryUpsert insert path, update path with title + status flipping through ConflictPolicy, applyRealtimeInventoryDelete row removal, and garbage-JSON resilience (no crash, no orphan row). The supabase-swift channel + status streams aren't hermetically testable without spinning up a real Realtime socket — first TestFlight build is the live verification.

userStories.title: Pricing model overview — FlipDesk subscription + GradeThread per-grade
userStories.description:
As a stakeholder, I need the canonical pricing model documented so every downstream story (US-201 → US-225) has a single source of truth. Two products billed on one Stripe customer: (1) FlipDesk subscription with four tiers, (2) GradeThread pay-per-grade with optional credit packs.

FLIPDESK TIERS (monthly / annual ≈ 17% off):
  • Free          $0          25 active listings, eBay only,  25 AI actions/mo,   3 included Standard grades/mo
  • Starter      $29 / $290   250 active listings, eBay + 1,  200 AI actions/mo, 10 included Standard grades/mo
  • Pro          $59 / $590   1,000 active listings, all marketplaces, 1,000 AI/mo, 30 included Standard grades/mo, bulk actions, scheduled actions, comp pulls
  • Business     $99 / $990   Unlimited listings, sub-accounts, API access, 5,000 AI/mo, 75 included Standard grades/mo, payout reconciliation, priority support

GRADETHREAD PER-GRADE:
  • Standard $2.99 (48h SLA)
  • Premium  $7.99 (12h SLA)
  • Express  $12.99 (1h SLA)

CREDIT PACKS (1 credit = 1 Standard grade; Premium = 3 credits; Express = 5 credits; credits never expire):
  • 10 credits   $24.99   ~17% off
  • 25 credits   $59.99   ~20% off
  • 50 credits  $109.99   ~26% off
  • 100 credits $199.99   ~33% off

Debit precedence on a submission: (1) included monthly grades (if subscriber and not exhausted, Standard only), (2) credit balance, (3) one-time Stripe Checkout for the chosen tier.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/PRICING.md exists with the table above as the human-readable canonical doc
PLAN_MATRIX object in src/lib/constants.ts mirrors the same numbers (any change to constants requires updating the doc in the same PR)

All competitor benchmarks captured (List Perfectly $29/$49/$69/$99, Vendoo $14.99/$29.99/$59.99/$99.99/$149.99, PSA $25/$50/$150/$300, LegitGrails $15-55) referenced in docs/PRICING.md as an appendix so future tweaks have context
Upgrade triggers documented: 80% of any cap fires soft modal; 100% hard-blocks the action with an upgrade CTA

Self-serve actions documented: upgrade (immediate prorated), downgrade (period-end), cancel (period-end → free), pause (1/2/3 months via Stripe pause_collection), annual switch (prorated), credit top-up (immediate)
Refund policy documented: 14-day money-back on first subscription invoice only; credit packs non-refundable but credits never expire

charge.refunded: insert ledger reversal for credit packs (delta = -credits, reason='refund'); for subscriptions, no DB change beyond the event log (Stripe handles it)

If a user buys a pack mid-flow, on return from Stripe Checkout the submission auto-retries the precedence and proceeds without a second click
Telemetry: posthog events 'grade.paid' with method label; 'grade.pack_upsell_shown' / 'grade.pack_upsell_converted'

userStories.title: Security: Content-Security-Policy + HSTS on the SPA (Cloudflare Pages)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the static frontend to ship a strict CSP and HSTS via public/_headers so an injected script cannot exfiltrate user data or tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: public/_headers adds Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy 'same-origin' to the global block (alongside the existing X-Frame-Options / X-Content-Type-Options / Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy)

A Content-Security-Policy scoped to known origins: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.gradethread.com https://functions.gradethread.com https://*.stripe.com https://*.ingest.sentry.io https://us.i.posthog.com; script-src 'self' https://js.stripe.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https:; frame-src https://js.stripe.com https://hooks.stripe.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
Ship for one deploy cycle as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, capture violations, then flip to enforcing
Verified in a browser that Stripe Checkout, Google OAuth redirect, Sentry, and PostHog all still function under the enforced policy
No 'unsafe-eval'; if a dependency requires it, document the exception in the PR instead of silently adding it
userStories.notes: Implemented (report-only phase): public/_headers global block gains Strict-Transport-Security (2y, includeSubDomains, preload), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin, and Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only scoped to the app's real origins — Supabase (api.gradethread.com), edge (functions.gradethread.com), Stripe (js/api/hooks), Sentry (*.ingest.sentry.io), PostHog (us.i + us-assets), Google Fonts (googleapis/gstatic), Google Analytics (googletagmanager + *.google-analytics.com). object-src none, base-uri/form-action self, frame-ancestors none, worker-src 'self' blob:. CAVEATS before flipping to enforcing CSP: (1) index.html has an INLINE gtag bootstrap script (lines 36-41) — script-src intentionally omits 'unsafe-inline' so it reports as a violation; externalize it or add a sha256 hash/nonce before enforce. (2) style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' (Tailwind/runtime style injection). (3) Needs a real browser pass (Stripe Checkout, Google OAuth redirect, Sentry, PostHog, GA) to confirm no legit resource is missing, then rename the header to Content-Security-Policy. Could not browser-verify locally. FLIPPED TO ENFORCING (2026-06-02): externalized BOTH inline-script blockers to /head-init.js (the gtag Consent-Mode bootstrap AND the font preload's inline onload= handler — the notes only flagged the first; the second would also have violated a strict script-src). index.html now loads <script src=/head-init.js> + the async gtag.js; head-init.js sets window.gtag/dataLayer + consent defaults and injects the Inter stylesheet via createElement (CSP-safe, still non-render-blocking). Renamed the header Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only -> Content-Security-Policy and added report-uri /csp-report + report-to + a Reporting-Endpoints header; new functions/csp-report.ts Pages Function logs violations so a missed origin surfaces in prod logs. Completed a full static origin audit — script-src (self+stripe+gtm+posthog-assets), connect-src (supabase api+wss, functions, *.stripe, *.ingest.sentry, posthog us+us-assets, GA hosts), style-src (self+unsafe-inline+gfonts), font-src, frame-src (stripe), worker-src blob — covers every third-party the codebase loads (loadStripe, gtag, posthog us.i default, Sentry bundled->ingest, GA). Build proof: scanned all 24 prerendered HTML files — ZERO inline executable scripts (script-src 'self' satisfied); no unsafe-eval. tsc+build green, vitest 138/138. RESIDUAL (operator, can't run a browser in-sandbox): post-deploy smoke test of Stripe Checkout / Google OAuth / Sentry / PostHog / GA, backstopped by the /csp-report sink — a miss is a one-line _headers add. passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: distributed + broadened rate limiting
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need rate limits that survive restarts, apply across all container replicas, and cover unauthenticated abuse - not just a per-process in-memory Map keyed by userId.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the in-memory Map in services/edge-functions/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts with a shared store (a Postgres rate_limit_counters table using an atomic increment RPC, or Deno KV) so counts hold across restarts and horizontal replicas
Key by userId when authenticated; fall back to client IP (CF-Connecting-IP, then validated X-Forwarded-For) for unauthenticated/pre-auth requests

Extend coverage in main.ts to /api/payments/*, POST /api/keys (stricter cap on key creation), /api/workspace/* invitation sends, /api/notifications/*, /api/flipdesk/ebay/oauth/start, /api/flipdesk/images/*, /api/flipdesk/reconciliation/*, /api/flipdesk/sheets/*, /api/content/scheduler/*
A coarse per-IP ceiling on all unauthenticated paths (including webhook receivers) to blunt floods
Continue emitting X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After; return 429 on exceed; fail-open only if the backing store itself is unreachable, and log that to Sentry
userStories.notes: Implemented: migration 00045_rate_limit_counters.sql (table + increment_rate_limit() RPC: atomic upsert, self-pruning of older windows, RLS service-role-only). Rewrote middleware/rate-limit.ts from the in-memory Map to the Postgres-backed fixed-window store — survives restarts + shared across replicas. Keyed by user:<id> when authed, else ip:<CF-Connecting-IP|XFF>. Added a per-group `scope` arg so budgets don't bleed across endpoint groups. FAIL-OPEN on any store error (never locks out traffic). Broadened coverage in main.ts: payments(30), api-keys(30), workspace(30), notifications(60), ebay-oauth-start(10), flipdesk images/recon/sheets(30 each), content-scheduler(60), plus a coarse per-IP 600/min ceiling on the unauthenticated /api/webhooks/* and /api/flipdesk/webhooks/* receivers (429 → provider retries, safe given US-277 idempotency). DECISION: chose Postgres over Deno KV (local Deno KV is per-container = same flaw as in-memory; the shared Supabase DB is the real cross-replica store). CAVEAT: adds one indexed upsert per rate-limited request; needs runtime verification (no Deno locally) — watch that the RPC latency is acceptable and that no legit flow trips a limit. VERIFIED (2026-06-02): confirmed migration 00045 (rate_limit_counters + atomic self-pruning increment_rate_limit RPC, RLS service-role-only) and the broadened main.ts coverage (payments/keys/workspace/notifications/oauth-start/images/recon/sheets/content-scheduler + coarse 600/min per-IP ceilings on both webhook receivers). REFACTORED rate-limit.ts to take an injectable incrementer with a LAZY supabase default, so the module is import-safe without a DB and the limiter is unit-testable in CI. Added rate-limit_test.ts (7 cases): under-limit + X-RateLimit headers, 429 + Retry-After on exceed, scope isolation, user-vs-IP keying, CF-Connecting-IP precedence, no-subject pass-through, and fail-open on store error. Edge suite 97 passed/0 failed. passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: request body-size limits + schema validation on edge inputs
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every edge endpoint to reject oversized or malformed payloads so a single request cannot exhaust memory or smuggle unexpected fields into a service-role query.
acceptanceCriteria: A body-size guard rejects requests exceeding per-route caps (e.g. 15MB for image/grade uploads, 256KB for JSON-only endpoints) with HTTP 413 before the body is fully buffered
zod schemas added for the request body of every POST/PATCH handler under services/edge-functions/src/routes/*; invalid input returns 400 with field errors, never a 500
Content-Type is enforced (application/json or multipart where expected)
Base64 image inputs are validated for declared MIME and decoded byte size before being forwarded to Claude Vision
A shared validation helper keeps handlers terse; at least the grade-submit and flipdesk grading-submit paths are converted as the reference implementation
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) Body-size guard: src/middleware/body-limit.ts rejects oversized payloads with HTTP 413 via the Content-Length header before the handler buffers the body; per-route caps resolved by path (15MB for image upload prefixes /api/grade, /api/v1/grades, /api/flipdesk/{grading,images,disclosure,autolister}, /api/content/images; 256KB for all other JSON-only /api/* endpoints). Registered once as app.use('/api/*', bodyLimit) after securityHeaders; /health + OPTIONS preflight exempt. (2) Shared validation helper src/lib/validation.ts: validateJson(c, zodSchema) enforces application/json Content-Type (415 otherwise), parses safely (400 on bad JSON), runs the schema and returns 400 with flattened field errors (never 500). zod added to deno.json import map (esm.sh/zod@3.23.8). (3) Reference conversions: flipdesk grading /submit and /validate now validate through a strict zod schema (items[].inventory_item_id UUID + tier enum, .strict() rejects smuggled fields, 1..200 batch bound), replacing the hand-rolled parseSubmitBody. (4) Base64 image inputs: decodeBase64Image() validates declared MIME against an allowlist, checks base64 charset, enforces decoded byte size BEFORE allocation, and sniffs magic bytes to confirm the bytes match the declared MIME; wired into api-v1 /grades before forwarding to storage/Claude Vision. userStories.title: Security: OAuth state CSRF hardening
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the eBay OAuth flow's state token to be single-use, short-lived, and user-bound so a callback cannot be forged or replayed.
acceptanceCriteria: oauth_states rows carry user_id, created_at, and expires_at (<=10 min); the eBay callback rejects missing, expired, or already-consumed state with 400
The state row is deleted (or marked consumed) atomically on successful token exchange; any reuse is rejected
The generated state value carries >=128 bits of CSPRNG entropy
The pattern is documented for reuse by future marketplace OAuth flows (Shopify / Whatnot)
userStories.notes: Mostly pre-existing + hardened. oauth_states (migration 00030) already has user_id/created_at/expires_at; the eBay callback does an atomic delete+select (single-use, replay-safe) and rejects expired/invalid state; generateState() uses crypto.getRandomValues(32 bytes)=256-bit CSPRNG (exceeds 128-bit req). FIXED an open-redirect: redirect_to was taken unvalidated at /oauth/start and appUrl() passes absolute http(s) URLs through as-is, so ?redirect_to=https://evil.com bounced the user off-site after the eBay round-trip. Added sanitizeRelativePath() (same-origin relative paths only), applied at /oauth/start (source) and in the callback (defense-in-depth), and set expires_at explicitly to now+10min (overrides the 15-min default). Pattern reusable for future marketplace OAuth. VERIFIED (2026-06-02): /oauth/callback consumes oauth_states via an atomic delete+select().maybeSingle() (single-use, replay -> invalid_state); expires_at checked (set to now+10min at /oauth/start); generateState() = 32-byte (256-bit) crypto.getRandomValues CSPRNG; sanitizeRelativePath() blocks absolute/protocol-relative redirect_to at both /oauth/start and the callback (defense-in-depth open-redirect fix). All AC met. passes=true.

VERIFIED (2026-06-02): migration 00044 processed_webhook_events (PK provider+event_id, RLS service-role-only deny-all, processed_at cleanup index). claimWebhookEvent() insert-on-conflict (23505 -> duplicate, fail-open on unexpected DB error). Stripe handler claims by event.id AFTER signature verification and BEFORE the dispatch switch (webhooks.ts:70); eBay handler claims by notificationId before side effects (flipdesk-webhooks.ts:169). Replay/duplicate never reaches a side effect, satisfying the exactly-once guarantee. userStories.title: Perceptual-hash photo-reuse & duplicate detection
userStories.description: As the platform, I want to fingerprint every uploaded grading photo with a perceptual hash and detect when the same image is reused across submissions or sellers, so that stolen listings, recycled photos, and stock images are flagged for review instead of being graded as a fresh item.
acceptanceCriteria: A perceptual hash (pHash/dHash) is computed for each grading image at ingest and stored with the image record
On submission, near-duplicate matches against prior images are detected via Hamming distance within a tunable threshold (robust to our compression/resize)
A match to a DIFFERENT user/submission flags the submission for review with the matched reference(s); a match to the SAME user's prior item is informational (legit relist)
Cross-tenant matching is privacy-careful: only an internal flag + reference id is surfaced to admins/owner, never another user's identity or photo to the submitter
Hashing + distance logic is unit-tested with transformed (resized/recompressed) copies; tenant isolation preserved

Pure hammingHex unit-tested (photo-reuse_test.ts). Threshold tunable via GRADING_REUSE_MAX_HAMMING (default 10). NOTE: FlipDesk item_photos use a separate uploader and are out of scope here. BUILD-NEW. Stronger 'stolen/stock photo' signal than EXIF and fully under our control.

userStories.title: Make the rate limiter trustworthy (CF-only origin; fail-closed on abusable routes)
userStories.description: As the platform, rate limiting must not be bypassable via spoofed IP or disabled by a DB blip, so abuse of webhooks, OAuth start, and the public API is actually throttled.
acceptanceCriteria: Origin is reachable only via Cloudflare so CF-Connecting-IP is trusted, or X-Forwarded-For is no longer trusted
The most abusable unauthenticated routes fail-closed (or use a local fallback) when the counter store is down
Traefik/Coolify direct reachability is verified closed
userStories.notes: [P2][Security] DONE 2026-06-09. Hardened services/edge-functions/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts. AC1 (spoofable subject): X-Forwarded-For is NO LONGER trusted as a rate-limit subject in production (clientIp() returns only the unspoofable CF-Connecting-IP; XFF kept solely as a dev/local convenience when !isProduction). An attacker rotating XFF can no longer mint per-IP buckets or evade limits. AC2 (fail-closed): rateLimiter() gained opts.failClosed; the abusable UNAUTHENTICATED webhook receivers (/api/webhooks/*, /api/flipdesk/webhooks/*) now run fail-closed — a counter-store outage drops to a process-local per-replica fallback counter (degraded ceiling, never UNLIMITED) and a header-stripped request is bucketed into a shared 'ip:unattributed' counter instead of waved through. The bulk of (authenticated) routes stay fail-OPEN for availability. AC3 (CF-only origin): added an OPTIONAL CF_ORIGIN_SECRET code belt — when set, CF-Connecting-IP is trusted only if the request carries the matching cf-origin-secret header Cloudflare injects (constant-time compare), so a direct-to-origin request can't pass off a forged CF IP; inert (network layer trusted) when unset. The remaining AC3 task is an OPS verification: Coolify/Traefik must reject non-Cloudflare traffic at the network layer (firewall to CF IP ranges or a cloudflared tunnel) — documented for deploy, not code. Tests: src/tests/rate-limit_test.ts extended with 6 cases (XFF distrust, fail-closed local fallback vs fail-open, unattributed shared bucket, CF_ORIGIN_SECRET trust). Verified via `deno lint` (clean) + standalone logic harness; `deno check`/`deno test` run in CI (security.yml deno-check) — this sandbox blocks egress to deno.land/esm.sh so deps can't be fetched locally.

userStories.title: Guard admin MFA enforcement flag + claims-decode coupling

(1) Startup assertion assertAdminMfaConfig() (env.ts) THROWS in production when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED=false unless an explicit ADMIN_MFA_ENROLLMENT_WINDOW=true escape hatch is set (which logs loudly); wired into main.ts before Deno.serve so a misconfigured prod deploy crashes instead of serving admin routes without AAL2. userStories.title: Tighten CSP and remove the inline-hash footgun
userStories.description: As the platform, the CSP should minimize exfiltration surface and not break when the inline head script changes, so XSS is harder and Consent Mode/GA don't silently break.

userStories.title: Standardize edge error responses and redact logs
userStories.description: As the platform, clients must receive safe generic errors and logs must not leak PII/secrets, so internal details and customer data are not disclosed.

(3) New middleware/access-log.ts replaces Hono logger(): logs only method+pathname(no query)+status+duration, NEVER request headers, so Authorization/X-API-Key/signatures can't leak; pathname run through redact(). userStories.title: Verify open-redirect safety of OAuth relative-path sanitizer
