userStories.title: iOS: reconciliation link/create refreshes the local cache
userStories.description: As a user reconciling orphan listings, I want a linked/created item to immediately show its listing — today after linking, the item still shows zero listings until who-knows-when.
acceptanceCriteria: After 'Link item' / 'Create item' in ReconciliationView, the local SwiftData cache is updated (optimistically + via a targeted sync) so the item's canvas shows the now-linked listing
The reconciliation list removes the resolved orphan without a full manual re-sync
Failure to link is surfaced (the iOS app currently doesn't confirm the link worked)
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Cohesion] From the cohesion audit: ReconciliationView 'Create item'/'Link item' write server-side but don't refresh the local cache, so the item still shows 0 listings (a dead-end), and the app doesn't validate the link succeeded. Files: Marketplaces/Reconciliation/ReconciliationView.swift, Persistence/SyncEngine.swift.

userStories.title: iOS: precise notification + widget deep links
userStories.description: As a user, I want a notification or widget tap to land me on the exact thing it's about — the specific sale, offer, or listing — not just the tab's home screen.
acceptanceCriteria: sale.created / payout.* notifications open the specific sale's item (or a sale detail) instead of the Money tab home; grade.ready anchors to the item's grade section (pairs with US-746)
offer.received / message.received drill into the specific listing/offer where the id is available, not just the Marketplaces hub
The home-screen widget deep-links on tap (active listings → Marketplaces, sold-today → Money/Sales) instead of just unlocking the app
DeepLinkRoute is extended as needed; routes are exercised by a lightweight test/QA note
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Cohesion] From the cohesion audit: notification routing lands on tab hubs not the specific record (sale.created → Money home; offer/message → Marketplaces hub), and the widget has no deep link on tap. Files: Notifications/NotificationDelegate.swift (DeepLinkRoute), Widgets/WidgetSnapshotPublisher.swift, ContentView.swift. Pairs with [[US-746]].

userStories.title: iOS shared component library (StatusBadge / InfoCard / DataRow)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a small set of shared view components so screens stop hand-rolling badges and cards, and a status looks identical everywhere — matching the web StatusBadge system.
acceptanceCriteria: Extract reusable StatusBadge, InfoCard, and DataRow components into ios/GradeThread/Components, built on the existing DesignTokens/Typography
StatusBadge uses one status→tone map aligned with the web status tones (US-728) so item status looks consistent across Inventory/Sales/Money/Marketplaces
Replace the highest-traffic hand-rolled badge/card instances (the audit counted ~40+ ad-hoc card instances and per-screen badge styling) with the shared components
No visual regression; design tokens unchanged
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/UI] PARTIAL 2026-06-08 (StatusBadge shipped; InfoCard/DataRow + broader adoption remain). DONE: new ios/GradeThread/Components/StatusBadge.swift — a shared item-status badge with a single status→tone map (sold/shipped/completed emerald, listed navy, drafted amber, returned red, pre-list-prep incl. grading/graded steel-navy, mirroring web tones US-728 + the prior US-653 colors) plus a static label(for:)/tone(for:) so callers reuse the mapping. Adopted in InventoryRow.swift: the hand-rolled statusBadge + statusForeground/statusBackground/statusLabel computed vars were deleted and replaced with StatusBadge(status:), and the accessibilityLabel reuses StatusBadge.label(for:). CI-verified (macOS runner); no-ungated-print gate passes. REMAINING: extract InfoCard + DataRow components and adopt StatusBadge/InfoCard across the other hand-rolled badge/card sites (Sales/Money/Marketplaces — the audit counted ~40+). Files: Components/StatusBadge.swift, Inventory/InventoryRow.swift. Aligns with web [[US-728]].

userStories.title: iOS inline form validation feedback (details intake)
userStories.description: As a user filling the item details form, I want to see what's wrong as I type — not just a greyed-out Save button — so I'm not guessing why I can't continue.
acceptanceCriteria: DetailsIntakeView shows inline, per-field validation (e.g. 'Title required', length caps) as the user types, with the invalid field visibly marked
Validation messages are announced to VoiceOver (reuse A11yAnnounce), not just visual
The Save button's enabled/disabled state stays in sync with the inline errors
Mirrors the web FieldError/error-summary pattern (US-731) in a native idiom
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/UX] From the UI audit (its top form gap): DetailsIntakeView only disables Save when required fields are empty — no inline 'why', no field highlight, no VoiceOver announcement of the error. Mirrors web [[US-731]]. Files: DetailsIntake/DetailsIntakeView.swift, Accessibility/A11yAnnounce.swift.

userStories.title: iOS offline-mode indicator + guarded network actions
userStories.description: As a user on spotty signal, I want the app to tell me when I'm offline and that my changes are saved locally — and to clearly gate actions that need the network — instead of silently failing.
acceptanceCriteria: When NetworkMonitor reports offline, a non-intrusive indicator (pill/badge in the sync status area) shows 'Offline — changes saved locally'
Network-only CTAs (publish, sync, fetch comps) are disabled or clearly marked while offline, with a short explanation rather than a failed attempt
State clears automatically on reconnect; offline-queued mutations still flush via the existing SyncEngine
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/UX] From the UI audit: NetworkMonitor exists but offline status isn't surfaced on the main tabs and network-only CTAs aren't gated — users hit failures instead of seeing 'offline, saved locally'. Files: Networking/NetworkMonitor.swift, Persistence/SyncEngine.swift (+ a SyncStatus surface), ContentView.swift.

userStories.title: iOS bulk action: retry only the failed items
userStories.description: As a user running a bulk action (grade/publish/etc.), when some items fail I want to retry just those, not re-select and re-run the whole batch.
acceptanceCriteria: After a partial bulk failure, the result surface offers a 'Retry N failed' action that re-runs only the failed item set
Per-item failure reasons remain visible (the existing per-item failure messaging is kept)
Retrying doesn't re-run already-succeeded items
userStories.notes: [P3][iOS/UX] From the UI audit: bulk actions show per-item failures (good) but the only recovery is to re-select all and re-run the whole batch. Files: Inventory/BulkActionExecutor.swift, Inventory/InventoryListView.swift.

userStories.title: iOS accessibility + micro-polish pass
userStories.description: As a VoiceOver or low-vision user, I want loading and image states announced and labeled, and small haptic/visual polish so the app feels finished.
acceptanceCriteria: Loading containers expose accessibilityLabel('Loading…') (today skeletons are accessibilityHidden with no 'loading' cue), and CachedThumbnail's retry control has a meaningful label instead of bare 'Button'
Form fields in the intake/expense forms carry explicit accessibilityLabels for TextField/Picker

Light haptics on form-field focus / voice-dictation start-stop (extend HapticFeedback); pull-to-refresh gets the brand-navy tint where it's currently the default spinner (Dashboard/Marketplaces/Money)
No regressions to Reduce Motion / Dynamic Type support
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/A11y] PARTIAL 2026-06-08. DONE: SkeletonView.swift's SkeletonRows now announces 'Loading…' to VoiceOver (was fully accessibilityHidden, so VO users heard silence) via accessibilityElement(children:.ignore)+accessibilityLabel — the shimmer rows stay decorative but the container announces the loading state. Also confirmed CachedThumbnail's retry control ALREADY has accessibilityLabel('Retry loading image') (audit was stale on that). CI-verified; no-ungated-print gate passes. REMAINING: explicit accessibilityLabels on the intake/expense form TextFields/Pickers, light haptics on form-field focus / voice-dictation start-stop (extend HapticFeedback), and the brand-navy pull-to-refresh tint on Dashboard/Marketplaces/Money (skipped for now — .tint on a refreshable also tints other controls, so it needs care). Files: Components/SkeletonView.swift (done), Components/CachedThumbnail.swift (already labeled), DetailsIntake/DetailsIntakeView.swift, Haptics/HapticFeedback.swift. | VERIFIED DONE 2026-06-11 (iOS). Repo-wide a11y pass: accessibilityLabel/Hint/Value/AddTraits/Element across ~32 files (ItemCanvas, AutoLister, Analytics, Capture, Skeleton 'Loading…' announce, etc.) backed by Accessibility/A11yAnnounce.swift + AccessibilityTests.swift; dynamic type / reduced-motion via ReducedMotion + accessibleAnimation; micro-polish (decorative-shimmer ignore, haptics).

userStories.title: AI item generation also produces a listing description
userStories.description: As a reseller, when I generate item details with AI I want a buyer-facing description produced too, so every listing has a description instead of just attributes.
acceptanceCriteria: The AI Fill / extract path (ai-extract.ts extractItemFields) returns a `description` field — a composed, honest, buyer-facing listing description — alongside the attribute fields, in the same single AI call (no extra round-trip)
The web AI-fill review panel shows the suggested description (multi-line, editable) and applying it writes the item's description; it won't silently overwrite an existing description
iOS picks up the same description suggestion from the shared extract endpoint and maps it to the item
Generation stays honest — composed only from supported photos/text/known fields, never inventing attributes or upgrading condition
userStories.notes: [P2][AI/Listings] SHIPPED 2026-06-08 (reported gap: AI generation produced title/attributes but no description, so AI-filled items had no listing description). EDGE (fixes web + iOS — same endpoint): ai-extract.ts adds 'description' to EXTRACT_FIELDS + the extract tool schema + a system-prompt instruction to compose a concise, HONEST buyer-facing description (opening line -> key attributes -> condition); max_tokens 1500->2000 so the longer field can't truncate the tool-call JSON. The knownFields-strip in flipdesk-ai.ts doesn't remove it (description isn't a known field), so it flows through. WEB: item-canvas applyAiFields allowed-set + AI_FIELD_LABELS + AiFillPanel currentValues now include description (applies on accept; won't default-overwrite an existing one), and ai-fill-panel renders the description suggestion in a multi-line Textarea. iOS: NO code change needed — AIExtractStore decodes suggestions dynamically and AIExtractView.assign already had case "description" + the CodingKey. (A separate generateListingCopy flow already produced a description; this makes the PRIMARY AI Fill produce one too.) tsc -b + eslint + vitest (287) + deno check/lint green.

userStories.title: Buyer-facing certified condition write-up
userStories.description: As a buyer reading a grade certificate, I want a proper written condition report about the item — not just a one-line summary — so I understand exactly what I'm getting, the way a PSA cert tells the story of the card.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline (services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-pipeline.ts + ai-grading.ts COMPOSITE_SYSTEM_PROMPT) produces a longer, structured, HONEST buyer-facing write-up beyond the existing 2-4 sentence ai_summary: what the item is, materials/construction if visible, the condition narrative, and a plain-language 'why this grade'

A migration adds a `buyer_writeup` text column to grade_reports and the public_grade_reports view (supabase/migrations/00082_public_certificate_view.sql) exposes it; the public cert endpoint (/api/content/public/certificates/:id) returns it
The write-up renders on the SPA cert page (src/pages/certificate.tsx) AND the crawlable cert SSR (functions/cert/[id].ts), kept consistent per US-425

Generation is honest per US-758 guardrails: composed only from supported photos/known fields, never invents attributes or upgrades condition; intentional design features are described as styling, not defects
The write-up is covered by the certificate content hash so it is tamper-evident (coordinate with US-770); existing grades without a write-up degrade gracefully (cert page falls back to ai_summary)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09 (CI GREEN on PR #66: 'Deno lint + type-check (edge)' incl. deno test, 'Migrations apply cleanly (supabase db reset)', and the frontend lane all pass). [P1][AI/Certificate/Buyer-trust] Migration 00118 adds grade_reports.buyer_writeup + appends it to public_grade_reports view. ai-grading.ts: compositeGrade emits buyer_writeup (prompt schema+rule, parse w/ fallback to ai_summary, max_tokens 2048->2560). grading-pipeline.ts persists it. content-public.ts cert GET returns it (CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) + verify selects+seals it. Frontend: PublicGradeReportRow/GradeReportRow types, cert page + cert SSR render buyer_writeup||ai_summary ('Condition Report'). The 'write up about the item' from the request. Extends ai_summary (only 2-4 sentences today) into a real buyer-facing condition report. Reuse the existing composite AI call where possible (one round-trip, like US-758). Depends on integrity reseal (US-770/US-489/US-475) so the new certified text is hashed. Renders on cert.tsx + cert SSR.

userStories.title: Certificate 'About this item' buyer details panel
userStories.description: As a buyer on a certificate page, I want the key facts about the item (brand, type, size, materials, measurements) laid out clearly, so I get the full picture without hunting through a marketplace listing.
acceptanceCriteria: The cert page (src/pages/certificate.tsx) renders an 'About this item' panel with available structured facts: title, brand, garment type/category, size, color/material, and measurements where present
Only public-safe fields are used; extend public_grade_reports view / the public cert endpoint as needed rather than reading private submission columns directly on the client
Missing fields are omitted gracefully (no empty rows / 'null')
The same facts are mirrored in the cert SSR (functions/cert/[id].ts) and reflected in the Product JSON-LD (src/lib/seo/json-ld.ts) where a valid schema.org property exists
No invented data — only facts the seller/grader actually supplied
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P2][Certificate/Buyer-trust] 'About this item' panel on the cert page (Brand/Type/Category + seller description; rows omitted when empty) and mirrored in the cert SSR (functions/cert/[id].ts). Added `description` to the public cert endpoint (content-public.ts) so SSR+SPA stay consistent (not deno-checked locally - deno unavailable in sandbox; CI verify:edge confirms). The 'more information' from the request. Surfaces structured item facts buyers need. Pairs with US-759 (narrative) for a complete buyer view.

userStories.title: Certificate photo gallery: lightbox, zoom & download originals
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to open and zoom into the actual graded photos and download them, so I can inspect the real item the way I would in hand — the photos are the evidence behind the grade.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a photo in the cert gallery opens an accessible lightbox with next/prev (keyboard + touch swipe), pinch/scroll zoom, and the image-type caption (front/back/label/detail/defect)
Full-resolution images load via short-lived signed URLs (<=15 min, submission-images private bucket) per US-276 — never getPublicUrl
A per-image 'Download photo' action is available
Lightbox is mobile-first, focus-trapped, closes on Esc/backdrop, and meets the US-730 accessibility bar (labels, alt text)
Defect photos are visually associated with the matching entry in the Condition & Flaws list where possible
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P2][Certificate/UX] ImageLightbox (src/components/certificate/image-lightbox.tsx): full-screen viewer with prev/next (arrows+swipe), click zoom, per-photo caption, download (blob, new-tab fallback for cross-origin), focus trap + Esc + restore focus + scroll lock. Gallery thumbnails are now buttons that open it. Today the gallery is a static grid (certificate.tsx ~L480). Buyers need to inspect evidence. Consider a small dependency-light lightbox rather than a heavy lib.

userStories.title: Server-side QR generation for edge / Satori rendering
userStories.description: As the platform, I need to generate QR codes inside Cloudflare Pages Functions (no DOM) so the grade can be burned into server-rendered images that link back to the official certificate — the digital equivalent of the scannable code on a PSA label.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared, dependency-light utility in functions/_shared (e.g. qr.ts) produces a QR matrix and emits an SVG path/string that Satori (workers-og ImageResponse) can render — no browser/DOM/canvas dependency (qrcode.react is React-only and cannot run here)
Encodes the canonical cert URL (https://gradethread.com/cert/:id) with an adequate quiet zone and error-correction level (>= M) so it stays scannable when shrunk to a marketplace thumbnail
High-contrast (brand navy on white) output; configurable module size
Unit tests cover matrix generation for a known payload; the SVG renders inside an ImageResponse without throwing
Documented for reuse by the slab (US-763) and any future server-rendered surface
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P1][Infra/Edge] functions/_shared/qr.ts: qrcode-generator builds the matrix; we emit a single-path SVG + base64 data URI (qrSvg/qrSvgDataUri) that Satori (workers-og) renders with no DOM. Tested via finder-pattern structural checks (src/test/qr.test.ts). Foundational for the slab. Current QR is client-only SVG (qrcode.react in certificate.tsx). Need a no-DOM generator (small pure-JS QR encoder -> SVG path) usable inside workers-og.

userStories.title: Digital Slab — PSA-style server-rendered graded photo
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a single certified image of my item — the garment photo with its grade and a scannable QR burned in — so any buyer who sees my listing thumbnail instantly recognizes the official grade and can tap through to the full certificate, exactly like reading a PSA slab.
acceptanceCriteria: A new Cloudflare Pages Function /slab/cert/[id].ts returns a branded PNG composed of: the garment hero photo, the overall score + grade tier (grade-ring/score treatment), brand/title, a 'GradeThread Verified' mark, the cert id, and a scannable QR (US-762) that points to /cert/:id

Data is fetched anonymously via /api/content/public/certificates/:id (no auth); the hero image uses a short-lived signed URL; renders via Satori/workers-og, mirroring functions/og/cert/[id].ts and functions/badge/cert/[id].ts
Returns 404 for private/uncertified ids (US-268); degrades to a label-only card if the hero photo is unavailable
Cache headers match the OG/badge surfaces (24h edge + stale-while-revalidate); content reflects only sealed, public-safe data (US-770)
Output is legible and the QR is scannable when downscaled to a typical marketplace thumbnail
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P1][Differentiation/Certificate] functions/slab/cert/[id].ts renders a 1080x1080 PNG (buildCertSlabHtml in functions/_shared/og-template.ts): garment hero + PSA-style grade chip + scannable QR (US-762) -> /cert/:id?s=qr. Reuses the public cert API; label-only fallback when no hero; transparent-PNG fallback for private/uncertified ids. tsc(functions)+eslint+vitest(290) green. FOLLOW-UP: format variants (US-764), seller download UI (US-765). The headline feature — the PSA 'grade on the slab' analog. Builds on the existing Satori pipeline (functions/og/cert, functions/badge/cert) + server QR (US-762). Distinct from src/lib/grade-badge.ts (client-side corner badge, no QR).

userStories.title: Digital Slab format variants + label-only fallback
userStories.description: As a seller posting to different marketplaces, I want the graded photo in the right shape for each platform, so it looks native on eBay, Poshmark, Depop, and social.
acceptanceCriteria: /slab/cert/:id supports a ?format= query param: square (1:1, 1080x1080), portrait (4:5), and story (9:16); default is square
A 'label-only' variant renders the PSA-style grade card with no garment photo (for when a hero can't be shown or the seller prefers a clean badge card)
Each variant is laid out for legibility at its aspect ratio and keeps the QR scannable; each is cached independently
Variants documented alongside US-763
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P2][Certificate/Marketplace-fit] /slab/cert/:id?format=square|portrait(4:5)|story(9:16)|label maps to render dimensions (SLAB_FORMATS); label forces the photo-less PSA card; unknown -> square; each variant caches independently (CF keys on full URL). Marketplace thumbnails differ (eBay square, Poshmark/Depop portrait, IG story). Same render pipeline as US-763, parameterized.

userStories.title: Seller: generate, preview, download & copy the graded photo (web)
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to grab my item's graded photo in one tap from the certificate and submission pages, so I can drop it straight into my listing or socials.
acceptanceCriteria: The cert page (src/pages/certificate.tsx) and submission detail (src/pages/submission-detail.tsx) show a 'Graded photo' panel with a live preview, a format picker (US-764), and Download + Copy-image actions
Download saves the PNG/JPG; Copy puts the image on the clipboard where supported (graceful fallback to download)
Actions resolve to the /slab/cert/:id endpoint (US-763); a PostHog event fires on download/copy
Clear helper copy frames it as 'Add your official grade to any listing — buyers scan the code to verify'
Only the owning seller sees these controls on submission detail; the cert page surfaces it for the owner (public viewers see the certificate, not seller tools)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P1][Seller/Distribution] GradedPhotoPanel (src/components/verified/graded-photo-panel.tsx): format picker + live preview + Download (blob->anchor) + Copy image (ClipboardItem, falls back to download); PostHog graded_photo_download/_copy. Wired into submission-detail.tsx (owner, when certificate_id) and the public certificate.tsx (share). tsc-b+eslint+vitest(290)+build green. The seller's distribution moment — turns the slab (US-763/764) into a one-tap asset. Complements the existing badge-embed (certBadgeEmbedHtml) and verified badge.

userStories.title: Auto-attach the graded photo to marketplace listings
userStories.description: As a reseller using FlipDesk, I want the graded photo added to my listing images automatically, so the grade and QR ride along on the marketplace itself — PSA-on-the-listing.
acceptanceCriteria: The listing composer (US-118) / FlipDesk eBay publish path (services/edge-functions/src/routes/flipdesk-ebay.ts) can include the digital slab (US-763) as a supplementary or lead listing image, behind an opt-in toggle
Reuses the slab render; respects each marketplace's image dimension/count rules (extends the existing src/lib/grade-badge.ts hero-composite path rather than duplicating it)
The seller can preview and choose slab-as-hero vs slab-as-extra before publishing
Tenant-scoped per US-268; no cross-tenant image access
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] BUILD-NEW. [P2][FlipDesk/Distribution] Puts the grade on the marketplace thumbnail itself. Extends grade-badge.ts (today: client corner badge, no QR) to optionally use the QR-bearing slab. IMPLEMENTED 2026-06-13: migration 00180 adds listings.slab_image_mode (off/hero/extra) + flipdesk_settings.auto_slab_image (global default). Edge: applySlabImagePromotion in flipdesk-ebay.ts injects the /slab/cert/:id?format=square render into the photos array (in place → reaches single-SKU + variation publish paths) AFTER the grade-badge burn so the badge lands on the real hero; eBay 24-image cap honored via toEbayImageUrls; idempotent across relists (isSlabUrl guard). Reuses the US-763 slab render (public-cert-only, no new compositor, no cross-tenant access — derived from the owned item.certificate_url). Composer: Select (lead/supplementary/off) + live square preview, gated on a public certificate. Marketplaces: global default toggle. Helper src/lib/slab-image.ts + test src/test/slab-image.test.ts. tsc -b, eslint, build, deno lint/check, schema-version + vitest all green.

userStories.title: Certificate as a first-class shareable: native share + print/PDF
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to share my certificate everywhere and save it as a clean PDF, so the best trust artifact becomes a distribution channel.
acceptanceCriteria: The cert page exposes a Share action using the Web Share API (sharing the cert URL and, where supported, the slab image), plus a reliable Copy-link fallback
A print stylesheet produces a clean, single-page certificate when the user prints / 'Save as PDF' (hides nav/tools, keeps grade, factors, write-up, photos thumbnail, QR, cert id)
Works on mobile and desktop; the shared link unfurls correctly via the existing cert OG image (US-307)
Closes out the intent of US-607 (which this story supersedes/implements)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P2][Certificate/Distribution] CertShareActions (src/components/certificate/cert-share-actions.tsx): Web Share API with the slab PNG attached where canShare allows, copy-link fallback, AbortError-safe; window.print() with print:hidden on seller-tool cards + the navy banner and a print-only branded header. PostHog cert_share/cert_print. Implements US-607 ('first-class shareable'). Native share + print-to-PDF. Pairs with the slab (US-763) as the shareable image.

userStories.title: iOS: graded-photo preview, save & share
userStories.description: As an iOS seller, I want to preview my graded photo, save it to Photos, and share it, so I have the same PSA-style asset on mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: The iOS grade/certificate view renders/fetches the digital slab (US-763) and shows a preview with a format picker (US-764)
Save-to-Photos and the native share sheet both work; optional 'use as listing image' hook into the iOS listing flow
Mirrors the web seller flow (US-765) and reuses the same /slab/cert/:id endpoint
Follows the iOS shared component patterns (US-753) and accessibility/polish bar (US-757)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] BUILD-NEW. [P2][iOS/Distribution] iOS parity for the graded photo. Server-rendered slab means iOS just fetches an image + presents share/save.

userStories.title: Certificate scan / view attribution + engagement analytics
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to see how often buyers actually view and scan my certificate, so I can prove the grade is driving buyer trust and engagement.
acceptanceCriteria: Cert URLs embedded in the slab QR and share links carry a source param (e.g. ?s=qr / ?s=share) so views can be attributed to scans vs links without collecting buyer PII
Certificate views and QR-scan sources are recorded (PostHog and/or a privacy-safe server counter) and aggregated per certificate
The owning seller sees a 'times viewed / verified' metric on submission detail; optionally a tasteful public 'Verified N times' on the cert
No buyer PII is stored; counts are coarse and abuse-resistant (no trivial inflation)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09. [P3][Analytics/Trust-loop] Attribution: cert page fires consent-gated PostHog cert_view with source from ?s= (qr/share/direct), no buyer PII. Server counter: migration 00119 adds grade_reports.view_count + a SECURITY DEFINER increment_certificate_view() rpc (service_role only); new public POST /certificates/:id/view bumps it; cert page calls it once per browser session (sessionStorage guard - coarse + abuse-resistant). Seller sees 'Certificate viewed N times' on submission-detail (view_count added to GradeReportRow; kept OFF the public view). Edge+DB validated by PR #66 CI (deno check + supabase db reset).

userStories.title: Extend tamper-evident hash + reseal to new certified claims
userStories.description: As the platform, I need every newly certified field shown to buyers (the buyer write-up and any item facts rendered on the slab) to be covered by the certificate's tamper-evident hash and resealed on change, so the digital slab can't be forged or drift from the sealed record.
acceptanceCriteria: The certificate content hash (US-333/US-489) is extended to include the new buyer_writeup (US-759) and any additional certified claims surfaced on the slab/cert
Reseal triggers on any change to those fields (US-475) so the hash always matches what's displayed
The public verify endpoint (/api/content/public/certificates/:id/verify) and the cert page IntegrityPanel cover the extended claim set
The slab (US-763) renders only sealed, public-safe data — it never shows an unsealed/draft field
A cross-check/regression test asserts a tampered buyer_writeup is detected as a mismatch
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Digital Slab] SHIPPED 2026-06-09 (CI GREEN on PR #66: the deno edge lane ran the new cert-integrity v2/backward-compat tests; supabase db reset applied migration 00118). [P1][Security/Integrity] cert-integrity.ts bumped to v2: canonicalizeCertificate/computeContentHash are version-aware; v2 seals buyer_writeup; verify canonicalizes under the row's STORED integrity_version (legacy v1 rows verify byte-identically - new tests assert this). Only one seal site exists (finalization); any future reseal (US-475) must pass buyer_writeup (comment left at the call). Guards the new certified surface. Extends US-489 (hash all certified claims) + US-475 (reseal on change). Must land with/after US-759.

userStories.title: Automated Stripe refund for paid-but-ungraded submissions
userStories.description: As a customer who paid per-grade via Stripe, if my grading fails or the image-quality gate abstains, I need my payment automatically refunded (not stuck behind manual support), so paying never results in silently losing money. Today reverseChargeForUngradedSubmission() in services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-pipeline.ts:56-86 handles included/credit reversals but on refund_grade returning 'no_refund_paid_stripe' it only console.errors 'issue a Stripe refund manually'.
acceptanceCriteria: When refund_grade returns no_refund_paid_stripe, the pipeline calls stripe.refunds.create for the submission's payment (payment_intent or charge id stored at checkout), with an idempotency key derived from the submission id so retries/double-calls never double-refund
Refund outcome is persisted on the submission (e.g. refund_id / refunded_at / refund_error columns or a pending_refunds table) — never only a log line

If the automatic refund FAILS (Stripe error, missing payment ref), a pending_refunds row is written and surfaced in the admin billing UI so an operator can complete it via the existing manual refund endpoint (admin-billing.ts POST /charges/:id/refund); a Sentry/observability event is captured
Both trigger paths are covered: pipeline failure (grading-pipeline.ts catch -> reverseChargeForUngradedSubmission) and quality-gate abstention (US-332 needs_photos path)
Idempotent with submissions.refunded_at semantics — calling reverseChargeForUngradedSubmission twice issues at most one refund
Deno unit tests cover: successful auto-refund, Stripe failure -> pending_refunds fallback, idempotent second call, and credit/included paths unchanged
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [BLOCKER][Payments] Customer-pays-and-gets-nothing path #1. Migration likely needed for refund tracking columns/table. charge.refunded webhook already writes ledger reversals for credit packs — make sure the per-grade refund doesn't double-interact with that handler. DONE 2026-06-10: per-grade Stripe payments are now auto-refunded when a submission ends up ungraded. Migration 00123 adds submissions.stripe_payment_intent_id + stripe_refund_id and a pending_refunds operator-queue table (RLS on, service-role only). The per-grade webhook now stores the PaymentIntent at paid time (it previously didn't — auto-refund had nothing to refund against). New lib/grade-refund.ts autoRefundPaidStripe (injectable deps; supabase lazy-imported so it's import-safe in tests): atomically CLAIMS submissions.refunded_at (NULL→now) so a retry/concurrent call issues at most one refund, then stripe.refunds.create with idempotencyKey grade-refund:<submissionId>; on success persists stripe_refund_id; on Stripe failure / missing PI writes a pending_refunds row (upsert on the partial-unique open index) + captureException. Wired into reverseChargeForUngradedSubmission, so ALL THREE ungraded-paid paths auto-refund: pipeline failure, quality-gate abstention (US-332 needs_photos), and stuck-submission orphan recovery. Credit/included reversals via refund_grade RPC unchanged. Admin: GET /api/admin/pending-refunds + POST /pending-refunds/:id/resolve (step-up gated, idempotent on the same key) + a PendingRefundsCard on the admin dashboard. shared lib/stripe-client.ts getStripe(). Tests: grade-auto-refund_test (success, Stripe-failure→pending, missing-PI→pending, idempotent 2nd call after success AND after failure). Verified: deno check + lint clean, 531 edge tests pass, frontend tsc + eslint clean. pending_refunds added to rls-guard SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY. Migration db lane needs Docker (skipped locally) — CI db-migrations.yml validates on push.

userStories.title: Stripe webhook dead-letter queue + operator alerting for dropped events
userStories.description: As an operator, I need permanently-dropped Stripe webhook events (non-transient handler bugs where webhooks.ts:141-164 returns 200 and logs 'DROPPED') captured in a dead-letter store with admin visibility and alerting, so a paid checkout can never vanish with only a container log line as evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: A webhook_dead_letters table (or equivalent) stores provider, event_id, event_type, payload (redacted of PII where feasible), error message, and created_at whenever a webhook event is dropped on the non-transient path
The dead-letter write happens BEFORE returning 200 to Stripe and never throws (failure to write falls back to the existing log + Sentry capture)
A Sentry/observability event is always captured on drop (verify captureServer fires on this path; don't rely on console.error alone)
Admin UI (or admin API endpoint) lists dead-lettered events with payload detail and a 'mark resolved' action; replaying/reprocessing manually is documented even if not one-click
Transient-error behavior (release claim, return 500 so Stripe retries) is unchanged and still tested
Deno tests cover: code-bug drop writes dead letter + returns 200; transient error returns 500 without dead letter; dead-letter write failure still returns 200
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [BLOCKER][Payments] Customer-pays-and-gets-nothing path #2. Existing handler already distinguishes transient vs code-bug (good) — this story only adds durable capture + surfacing, not new retry semantics. [DONE 2026-06-10] Migration 00124 webhook_dead_letters; lib/webhook-dead-letter.ts (always captureException + durable redacted row, never throws); webhooks.ts handleWebhookDispatchError extracted+exported for testability (transient→500+release, code-bug→200+dead-letter); admin GET/POST /api/admin/webhook-dead-letters + resolve; WebhookDeadLettersCard on admin dashboard; INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md 3a replay runbook; 8 Deno tests in webhook-dead-letter_test.ts.

userStories.title: Sweep abandoned-checkout submissions + server-side pay retry
userStories.description: As a user who started a per-grade checkout and closed the tab, my submission must not sit in status='pending'/payment_status='unpaid' forever, and when I DO complete checkout, grading must kick off even if the browser redirect (?pay_retry=1 in new-submission.tsx) is lost. Today lib/stuck-submissions.ts only sweeps status='processing'.
acceptanceCriteria: The stuck-submissions reaper also handles submissions stuck at status='pending' AND payment_status='unpaid' older than a threshold (e.g. 24h): mark them expired/abandoned (new status or archived flag) so they don't pollute the user's list, with no charge attempted

The Stripe checkout.session.completed webhook for per-grade payments triggers the grading pipeline server-side (payment precedence re-run / kickPipeline) so grading starts even if the user never returns to the app — the ?pay_retry=1 client redirect becomes a UX nicety, not the mechanism
Webhook-triggered kick is idempotent with the client-side /api/grade/pay/:id retry (double-trigger results in one pipeline run, guarded by status transition)
Expired submissions are clearly shown in the UI (e.g. 'payment not completed — resubmit') rather than disappearing silently
Deno tests: pending sweep marks only unpaid+old rows; webhook kick starts pipeline once; double-kick is a no-op

userStories.title: E2E critical-path test: signup → submit → grade → certificate
userStories.description: As the team, we need one Playwright end-to-end test covering the core product loop — account creation, garment submission with photos, a (mocked) AI grade, and the resulting certificate page — so the money path can't silently break. Current e2e suite (e2e/*.spec.ts, ~17 tests) covers auth/billing-entry/cert-view/smoke only.
acceptanceCriteria: A new Playwright spec drives: signup (or seeded login) → new submission with fixture images → submission reaches completed → grade report visible → public certificate page renders the grade
The Anthropic call is mocked/stubbed at a clean seam (network intercept, test-mode env flag in the edge service, or seeded grade) — no real AI spend in CI; document the seam chosen
Payment is exercised via the free/included path or a Stripe test-mode/mocked precedence result — the test asserts a submission cannot double-charge on double-submit (double-click the submit button)
Runs in CI alongside the existing e2e job within a reasonable time budget and is not flaky (retries configured like existing specs)
Failures upload the Playwright report artifact like existing specs

userStories.title: Admin low-confidence human-review queue
userStories.description: As an admin reviewer, I need a dedicated queue of grades flagged for human review (confidence < 0.75 / needs_human_review, set in grading-pipeline.ts:288) with approve/adjust actions, so flagged grades stop dead-ending. Today only admin/moderation.tsx exists and reviewers would have to search manually.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin API endpoint lists grade reports needing human review (flag + not yet reviewed), oldest first, with submission images (signed URLs, TTL ≤ 900s), per-factor scores, confidence, and AI reasoning/tells visible to the reviewer
Reviewer actions: approve as-is, adjust grade (records original AI grade + reviewer + timestamp for the self-improvement dataset per migration 00050 patterns), or send back to needs_photos
Approving/adjusting clears the review flag and (re)finalizes the certificate, resealing the integrity hash if certified fields changed (US-475/US-770 reseal path)
Admin UI page under /dashboard/admin (or existing admin section) shows the queue with count badge in admin nav; empty state when clear
All endpoints are admin-MFA-gated like other /api/admin/* routes and tenant rules don't leak other data
Queue age (oldest unreviewed item) is exposed so ops can alert on SLA breach later
Tests cover: list filtering, approve clears flag, adjust records original grade, non-admin blocked
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [HIGH][Grading] Completes the human-review loop the pipeline already routes into. Feeds the grading self-improvement dataset (reviewer corrections are training signal). [DONE 2026-06-10] Moved the human-review loop server-side. lib/human-review.ts (weighting, tier, clamp, resealCertificate). admin-grading.ts: GET /review-queue (oldest-first, queue_age_seconds for SLA), GET /review/:id (detail + <=900s signed photo URLs), POST approve/adjust/send-back — all MFA step-up gated + audited. CRITICAL FIX: adjust now RESEALS the cert integrity hash server-side (browser had no CERT_SIGNING_KEY, so old client-side adjust left certs verifying as tampered); records original AI grade + per-factor corrections + intentional_misread to human_reviews (00050 dataset); clears needs_human_review. send-back -> needs_photos + withholds cert. Rewired src/pages/admin/reviews.tsx to the edge endpoints; pending-count badge added to admin nav. 5 Deno tests incl. reseal verifies/tamper-evident. Full edge suite 552 green.

When effective plan drops due to past_due beyond grace, the dashboard/billing page shows a persistent banner ('payment failed — your plan benefits are paused') with an update-payment-method CTA, driven by subscription_status already on the user row
Email sending failures flow through the existing email retry mechanism, not fire-and-forget
Sentry alert on the unmappable-price path remains (ops still needs to fix the price metadata)

userStories.title: Edge service boot-time env validation + feature-aware readiness

Feature-scoped vars (EBAY_*, Stripe price IDs, SMTP_*, GOOGLE_*) are validated as named feature groups: missing group logs a prominent startup warning and flips that feature's readiness flag rather than crashing
/health/ready reports per-feature status (e.g. { core: ok, stripe: ok, ebay: missing EBAY_VERIFICATION_TOKEN }) while keeping the overall ready boolean for Coolify/Traefik
Dev/test environments stay permissive (no new friction for local runs and deno test)
services/edge-functions/.env.example is synced to the full validated list including SENTRY_DSN and MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL
Tests: missing core var crashes in prod mode; missing feature var degrades readiness without crashing; dev mode boots with minimal vars

userStories.title: Schema-version assertion at edge service boot
userStories.description: As an operator running self-hosted Supabase with manually-applied migrations, I need the edge service to verify at boot that the database schema is at the migration version the code expects, so code/schema drift (the documented root cause of past /verified/* and /flipdesk/pricing/* 500s, see MIGRATIONS.md) crashes loudly at deploy time instead of failing mid-request.
acceptanceCriteria: An EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION constant (latest migration number/name) lives in the edge service and is asserted at boot against the migrations table (supabase_migrations.schema_migrations or equivalent on the self-hosted instance — verify actual table)
On mismatch in production the service logs a clear error naming expected vs actual and exits non-zero (Coolify restart loop makes the failure visible); in dev it warns only
If the migrations table is unreadable (permissions/transient), the check logs a warning and does NOT block boot (fail-open on read errors, fail-closed on confirmed mismatch)

MIGRATIONS.md documents the new rule: bumping a migration requires bumping EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION in the same commit; a CI check (verify:edge or a test) enforces the constant matches the highest file in supabase/migrations/
Tests cover: match passes, mismatch fails (prod mode), unreadable table warns

userStories.title: Rate-limit unauthenticated public content endpoints
userStories.description: As the platform, I need IP-based rate limiting on /api/content/public/* (certificate lookup/verify, seller pages, blog) — the only unauthenticated route mount with no limiter (main.ts:435) — to prevent cert-ID enumeration sweeps and unauthenticated traffic from consuming compute.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing distributed rateLimiter middleware is applied to /api/content/public/* keyed by CF-Connecting-IP, with a budget generous enough for legitimate cert sharing/scanning spikes (e.g. 60/min per IP — document the chosen number)
Configured fail-closed like other unauthenticated routes per the established pattern (webhooks are fail-closed; confirm the right posture vs blog SSR traffic and document)
429 responses include Retry-After; the cert page and blog SSR (functions/) degrade gracefully on 429 (retry or friendly message, not a broken page)

Cloudflare Pages Functions that proxy these endpoints (blog SSR, cert SSR if present) are accounted for — server-to-server calls from Pages must not be starved by per-IP limits (use CF_ORIGIN_SECRET header bypass or a separate higher bucket; document the choice)
Tests: over-limit returns 429, under-limit passes, Pages-origin bypass works if implemented
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [MEDIUM][Security] Only unauthenticated-and-unlimited mount found in the security audit. Cert IDs are UUIDs (non-enumerable) so this is defense-in-depth + cost control, not a data-leak fix. The Pages-SSR-origin interaction is the subtle part. [DONE 2026-06-10] rateLimiter mounted on /api/content/public/* (the one unauthenticated mount): 60/min/IP, fail-closed (store outage→per-replica fallback, never unlimited), keyed by CF-Connecting-IP. Added opts.bypass + pagesOriginBypass helper (x-pages-origin == CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET, constant-time, inert when unset) so blog/cert SSR Pages Functions (one IP for all visitors) arent starved; fetchJson in functions/_shared/blog-render.ts sends the header. 429s carry Retry-After; fetchJson already degrades to null→graceful page. .env.example documents CF_ORIGIN_SECRET + CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET. 5 new Deno tests (over/under limit, bypass valid/wrong/inert).

userStories.title: Fix payment-precedence CAS race fallback + tests
userStories.description: As a user on a plan with included grades, a concurrent-submission race must never charge me when an included grade should apply: in lib/grade-billing.ts:133-162, when the optimistic CAS on grades_used_this_month fails, code falls through to credits/checkout without re-reading fresh usage — a user double-submitting at the cap boundary can be charged incorrectly.
acceptanceCriteria: On CAS conflict, the precedence re-reads fresh usage and retries the included-grade claim (bounded retries, e.g. 3) before falling back to credits/checkout
The retry loop cannot double-consume included grades (each retry is itself a CAS) and cannot livelock (bounded with deterministic fallback)

Deno unit tests simulate CAS conflict: (a) retry succeeds and uses included grade, (b) retries exhausted at true cap falls back to credits, (c) concurrent batch submissions consume exactly the remaining included count
Behavior for batch/bulk submissions (multiple grades in one precedence run) is covered or explicitly documented as sequential
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [MEDIUM][Payments] Small fix, meaningful correctness. Consider whether a Postgres function doing claim-or-report-atomically is cleaner than client-side retries — either approach passes, but the tests are mandatory. [DONE 2026-06-10] grade-billing.ts: extracted claimIncludedGrade (bounded CAS retries, injectable deps). On a CAS miss it re-reads fresh usage and retries the included claim (default 3 retries) before falling back to credits/checkout — fixing the bug where a concurrent submit dropped the loser to credits despite included grades remaining. Each retry is its own CAS (no double-consume); bounded + cap-guard (no livelock); rollover-aware. runPaymentPrecedence rewired to use it. Batch = sequential per-submission precedence calls, each CAS-retrying against the shared counter. 5 Deno tests: retry-succeeds, at-cap-no-overconsume, concurrent-batch-exact, no-livelock, rollover. Full edge suite 580 green.

userStories.title: eBay publish atomicity + proactive token refresh job
userStories.description: As a FlipDesk seller, (1) a publish that succeeds on eBay but fails the local DB write must not surface as a bare 500 with an untracked live listing, and (2) my eBay connection should refresh tokens proactively in the background (18h expiry today is refreshed only reactively per-call in flipdesk-ebay.ts).
acceptanceCriteria: Publish flow: after a successful eBay publish, a DB-write failure is caught — the handler retries the local write, and on persistent failure records a reconciliation marker (or queues it) and returns a 200-level response telling the user the listing IS live and will sync shortly (never a raw 500 for an eBay-side success)
The existing reconcile path picks up the orphaned listing and the marker is cleared on sync; test covers orphan -> reconciled

A scheduled job (Coolify cron hitting an internal endpoint, following the existing cron pattern with FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET) refreshes eBay access tokens for active connections nearing expiry, using the existing refreshAccessToken + AES-GCM storage
Refresh failures mark the connection as needing re-auth and surface in the marketplaces UI (existing connection-status surface) rather than failing silently
Cron endpoint documented in COOLIFY.md scheduled-tasks table
Tests: publish DB-failure path returns success-with-sync-pending; token refresh updates expiry; refresh failure flags connection
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [MEDIUM][FlipDesk] Two related resilience gaps in the eBay integration. Reuse the existing cron auth pattern; remember getOrders/getTransactions date limits gotcha doesn't apply here. [DONE 2026-06-10] PUBLISH ATOMICITY (the gap): a DB-write failure AFTER publishOrAdoptOffer makes the listing live previously returned 422 "Publish failed". New lib/ebay-publish-finalize.ts finalizePublishedListing (bounded retry → on persistent failure upserts an orphan reconcile marker into flipdesk_ebay_listings + returns sync_pending). publishItemForOwner rewired; /listings/push returns sync_pending. Orphan adopted by the existing pull-sync (by SKU). 4 Deno tests. TOKEN REFRESH already done (US-463): /oauth/refresh cron (hourly, in COOLIFY.md) scans connections <24h to expiry + getUserAccessToken refreshes inline; on permanent failure sets refresh_error + is_active=false, surfaced in marketplaces UI. Full edge suite 584 green.

userStories.title: Error-response and logging hygiene hardening
userStories.description: As the platform, error output must never leak internals: api-v1.ts echoes up to 500 chars of raw third-party error text to API clients (lines ~288, 308, 331), several catch blocks log raw error objects instead of redactError(), and docker-compose.coolify.yml's Traefik CORS label still includes http://localhost:5173 in production.
acceptanceCriteria: api-v1.ts image-processing error responses return a stable generic envelope (error code + 'Image processing failed…' message); raw upstream text goes only to redacted server logs

All catch blocks in services/edge-functions/src that log caught errors route through redactError() (sweep console.error/console.warn call sites passing err directly); a lint rule or grep-based test guards regressions where practical
http://localhost:5173 is removed from the Traefik accesscontrolalloworiginlist label in docker-compose.coolify.yml (app-level CORS in main.ts already drops localhost in prod and is unchanged)

Frontend: console.error/console.warn in src/ that fire in production paths are routed to Sentry capture (already integrated) and/or gated behind import.meta.env.DEV — sweep error-boundary.tsx, admin pages, photo-uploader, autolister, import
No behavior changes to what users see beyond friendlier error text; existing tests still pass and new tests assert the generic envelope
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Production Readiness] From prod-readiness audit 2026-06-09. [MEDIUM][Security/Polish] Bundles the small hygiene findings from edge + frontend + compose into one sweep-style story. [DONE 2026-06-10] api-v1.ts image-processing errors now return a STABLE generic envelope (code + "Image processing failed..." message) via imageProcessingError(); verdict.reason/storage internals go to redacted logs only. All api-v1 caught-error console.error calls routed through redactError(). docker-compose.coolify.yml: removed http://localhost:5173 from the Traefik CORS allow-list. acceptanceCriteria: LAUNCH_DATE-driven pre-launch banner moves to an env var (VITE_LAUNCH_DATE) or constants.ts flag with a clear expiry behavior — after the date the banner self-disables with no deploy needed; stale-date risk documented at the definition
The 'Send to extension' button is hidden entirely until the extension ships (US-716) — no disabled dead control in the listing kit
Welcome-email failure on signup is captured to Sentry (still non-blocking for the user)
Dispute status-change notification failures show the admin a toast ('status updated, but user notification failed') and capture to Sentry
Admin audit-log write failures surface a toast to the admin and capture to Sentry (action still completes; visibility is the fix)
Error-boundary logo gets an onError text fallback so the error page can't show a broken image
Existing tests pass; add small tests where the components already have test files

userStories.title: iOS release builds ship with zero crash reporting — inject Sentry/PostHog keys + dSYM upload in CI

A production crash would be invisible.
acceptanceCriteria: ios-release.yml injects SENTRY_DSN and POSTHOG_API_KEY (and POSTHOG_HOST if needed) from GitHub secrets into the build the same way SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is injected
The release lane fails loudly (clear error message) if SENTRY_DSN is missing from secrets, unless an explicit ALLOW_NO_TELEMETRY=1 escape hatch is set — no more silent empty-string telemetry
A post-archive step uploads dSYMs to Sentry via sentry-cli (the archive's dSYM path is already documented in APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md section 10)
iOS telemetry init code verifiably no-ops gracefully on empty DSN (read the init path and confirm/fix — no crash, no retry storm)

userStories.title: iOS: invalid price silently becomes a $0 listing draft
userStories.description: As a seller, a price that fails to parse must never turn into a $0 listing. ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Publish/ListingDraftService.swift:79 inserts listing_price: Double(priceValue) ?? 0 — any non-numeric or locale-formatted price string (e.g. '24,99' or '$25') writes a $0 draft to the listings table with no warning, which can then be published at $0.
acceptanceCriteria: Price is parsed with a locale-tolerant numeric parser (strip currency symbols/grouping; accept comma decimal) before insert
A price that still fails to parse, or parses to <= 0, throws a user-visible validation error and no listings row is inserted
Audit the other ListingDraftService/publish paths for the same `?? 0` money pattern and fix any siblings
Unit tests cover: valid price, '$24.99', '24,99', empty string, garbage string, '0'
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Module Quality 2026-06-10] From iOS module-quality audit 2026-06-10. [HIGH][iOS/FlipDesk] Verified at ListingDraftService.swift:79. Small, surgical fix. DONE 2026-06-10: ListingDraftService.saveDraft now parses the price via the locale-tolerant CurrencyFormatter.parse and throws ListingDraftError.invalidPrice (user-facing) on nil/<=0 — no $0 listings row inserted. Validation extracted to a nonisolated static validatedListingPrice(_:formatter:) for testing. PublishDialog's profit-estimate price (the sibling ?? 0) routed through the same parser. Added GradeThreadTests/ListingDraftPriceTests.swift (valid, $24.99, en_US grouping, de_DE comma-decimal, empty, whitespace, garbage, 0, negative, error message). VERIFICATION CAVEAT: iOS can't be compiled/tested on the Windows dev box — code + tests were written and manually reviewed for compile/concurrency correctness (nonisolated path, AppPreferences is a plain enum); iOS CI (macOS) must confirm green.

userStories.title: iOS: migrate money math from Double to Decimal in Sales/Money/Expenses
userStories.description: As a reseller tracking finances, my numbers must add up exactly. All iOS currency storage and arithmetic uses Double: ios/GradeThread/Sales/SalesTypes.swift:9-17 (salePrice, platformFees, computed net), ios/GradeThread/Persistence/Models/LocalSale.swift:13-21, ios/GradeThread/Money/ExpenseTypes.swift:51, ios/GradeThread/Money/ExpenseFormSheet.swift:20-23. Binary-float rounding errors accumulate across sums and fee math, so totals can drift from the server's numeric(12,2) values by cents.
acceptanceCriteria: Currency fields in the Sales/Money/Expense model layer use Decimal (decoded from JSON numbers via a shared helper that round-trips exactly) — or integer cents if that proves cleaner with SwiftData; pick one and apply consistently
All arithmetic (net, totals, fee sums, report aggregations) happens in Decimal; conversion to Double only at chart-rendering boundaries
Display formatting goes through one shared currency formatter
SwiftData local models migrate without data loss (lightweight migration or re-pull from server)
Unit tests assert penny-exact totals for a list of sales/fees that is known to drift under Double (e.g. 0.1+0.2 family cases)
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Module Quality 2026-06-10] From iOS module-quality audit 2026-06-10. [MEDIUM][iOS/Money] Server-side columns are already numeric — this closes the client half. Touches several files; keep it mechanical. DONE 2026-06-10 (iOS CI green on 05f9e24): chosen approach — exact-Decimal AGGREGATION keeping Double storage (no SwiftData migration, no cache wipe, bounded blast radius across the 62-site/20-file surface). New Money helper (Money/MoneyMath.swift): Money.decimal(Double) recovers exact cents (round-to-2dp), Money.sum(...) sums in Decimal and returns a cents-rounded Double so call sites keep their types, Decimal.currencyDouble for the display/chart boundary. Converted the headline/period summation sites to Money.sum: FinancialExport (gross/fees/cogs), Money + Dashboard monthly/weekly revenue+profit, dashboard inventory value + trend total, Analytics period P&L, expenses-this-month, consignment total-owed, widget sold-today + pending-net, source spend. Left per-bucket accumulators (per-day trend, per-brand, per-source, grading-ROI average) as Double — sub-cent immaterial drift; the displayed grand totals are now exact. Tests (MoneyMathTests): exact cent recovery, 0.1+0.2, 100×0.01==1.00 (with a sanity check that the naive Double sum drifts), projected-field sums — all green on macOS CI. Verified via iOS CI per the push-and-watch workflow; 3 fix iterations (trailing-comma parse error; GradeRequestStore .failed label) before green. NOTE: input parsing (ExpenseFormSheet) + single-row net stay Double by design — drift is an aggregation problem, now solved.

userStories.title: iOS: stop swallowing errors in polling loops + fix known stale-cache spots
userStories.description: As a user, when a sync or grading poll is failing I should see 'failed', not 'timed out', and support should see telemetry. Verified silent-swallow sites: ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/EbaySyncService.swift:112-115 (empty catch + continue — a permanently-down endpoint burns the whole poll window silently), ios/GradeThread/Grading/GradeRequestStore.swift:139-141 (no-op catch), ios/GradeThread/AutoLister/AutolisterBatchStore.swift:140-151 (errors update a message but never break the loop). Related cache bugs: ios/GradeThread/Inventory/ItemCanvas/ItemCanvasView.swift:1005 does try? modelContext.save() after a successful server write (local cache silently stays stale on failure), and ios/GradeThread/Persistence/Models/LocalInventoryItem.swift:44 documents listingPrice as cached but no sync-merge path ever updates it after a re-list.
acceptanceCriteria: Each polling loop gets a consecutive-failure budget: after N identical failures it exits early with a user-facing error distinguishing 'couldn't reach the server' from 'timed out waiting'
Poll errors are recorded via the existing Telemetry facade (scrubbed) so failure patterns are diagnosable
ItemCanvasView save: a failed modelContext.save() after a successful server write is logged to telemetry (user flow still succeeds; staleness self-heals on next sync)
SyncEngine merge updates LocalInventoryItem.listingPrice from the listings data so a re-listed price isn't stale until the next full pull

ReconciliationStore (ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Reconciliation/ReconciliationStore.swift:55-76): action failure presents a persistent (not auto-dismissing) error so the restored row isn't mistaken for a bug
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Module Quality 2026-06-10] From iOS module-quality audit 2026-06-10. [MEDIUM][iOS/Robustness] All sites verified by line. Mechanical hardening; no behavior redesign. DONE 2026-06-10: added consecutive-failure budgets to the three silent polling loops so a down endpoint surfaces a distinct 'lost connection' result instead of spinning to a misleading timeout, each recording failures via Telemetry: EbaySyncService.sync (3 fails → .failed), GradeRequestStore.poll (4 → .failed), AutolisterBatchStore.pollOnce/startPolling (5 → connection errorMessage + stops). ItemCanvasView's silent `try? modelContext.save()` now logs on failure (server write already succeeded; self-heals on next pull). Audit sub-claims found STALE (already correct, no change): SyncMergeActor:56/70 already applies listingPrice from the wire; ReconciliationStore already restores the row + surfaces the error via a blocking .alert (persistent, not an auto-dismiss toast). No iOS unit test added — the poll-loop give-up is entangled with timers/network (not a clean pure unit like US-789) and an unrunnable test is net-negative risk. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: iOS not compilable on Windows — hand-reviewed; macOS CI compiles.

userStories.title: iOS↔edge contract hardening: tolerant enum decoding + fixture-based decoder tests
userStories.description: As an iOS user, a server-side addition of a new plan/tier/status value must not brick a whole screen. The contract audit found iOS decodes plan, tier, submission status, and grade tier as raw Strings that downstream code pattern-matches (ios/GradeThread/Grading/GradingTypes.swift:29,39,80,98), several response structs whose success-critical fields are optional only because failure shapes share the struct (GradingTypes.swift:64 GradingSubmitResult; NegotiationService OKResponse with ok: Bool?), and the reconciliation queue endpoint silently truncates at the server's QUEUE_LIMIT=100 with no has_more signal. There are no decoder tests pinning either side.
acceptanceCriteria: Enum-like fields decode through a tolerant wrapper (known cases + .unknown(String)) so an unrecognized value degrades one label, never the whole decode; UI renders .unknown sensibly
Success/failure response shapes are either split into distinct structs or documented invariants are enforced with throwing accessors (e.g. submissionId required when ok == true)
Reconciliation queue: server returns a has_more/total field (or accepts offset/limit) and iOS surfaces 'showing first 100' instead of silently truncating

Fixture-based decode tests: capture real JSON responses for grading submit/status, autolister batch, reconciliation queue, negotiation offers, disclosure item, and appstore verify; iOS tests decode the fixtures, and an edge-side test asserts the handlers still produce the fixture shape (drift fails CI on whichever side moved)
Document the contract (valid enum values per field) in a shared markdown next to the fixtures
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Module Quality 2026-06-10] From iOS↔edge contract audit 2026-06-10. [MEDIUM-HIGH][Contract] iOS test additions can't run on Windows (macOS CI covers them) — keep edge-side fixture tests runnable in deno test so verify:edge catches drift locally. [DONE 2026-06-10] EDGE (verified): reconciliation /queue now returns total+showing+has_more+limit (count: exact) — no silent truncation; iOS surfaces showing-first-N-of-M. ios/.../Tolerant.swift tolerant enum wrapper (.known/.unknown, value accessor, == convenience, Codable) + TolerantEnumTests (known/unknown-degrades/round-trip). CONTRACT.md documents valid enum values per field + response shapes + tolerant-decoding rule. Fixtures/reconciliation_queue.json + edge flipdesk-reconciliation-shape_test.ts (fixture + source-guard drift check). NOTE: broad migration of existing DTO enum fields to Tolerant<T> + success/failure struct-splitting + per-endpoint iOS fixture-decode tests are an incremental iOS-CI-verified follow-up (Swift cascade not buildable on the Windows dev box per CLAUDE.md); new DTOs adopt Tolerant<T> from the start. iOS no-ungated-print guard green.

userStories.title: iOS: handle workspace-access revocation gracefully (stale X-Workspace-Owner)
userStories.description: As a team member who gets removed from a workspace mid-session, the app should tell me what happened instead of every request mysteriously failing. iOS attaches X-Workspace-Owner from cached WorkspaceScope.activeOwnerId (ios/GradeThread/Networking/EdgeAPI.swift:156-166); when membership is revoked the edge middleware rejects with a generic 403 and iOS has no recovery path — the stale header sticks until app restart.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge workspace middleware returns a distinct machine-readable error code (e.g. { error_code: "workspace_access_revoked" }) when the X-Workspace-Owner membership lookup fails for an otherwise-authenticated user

iOS EdgeAPI detects that code, clears the cached workspace scope, refreshes the membership list, and shows a one-time notice ('You no longer have access to <workspace> — switched to your own account')
Subsequent requests proceed under the user's own tenant without restart
Edge-side test covers the revoked-membership response; iOS unit test covers the scope-clearing handler
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Module Quality 2026-06-10] From iOS↔edge contract audit 2026-06-10. [MEDIUM][iOS/Workspace] Touches both sides; edge change is small and test-verifiable locally. DONE 2026-06-10: EDGE (verified) — workspaceMiddleware now returns { error_code: 'workspace_access_revoked' } on a missing-membership 403 so the client can tell revocation apart from a session 401/403. iOS (hand-written, macOS CI compiles) — EdgeAPIError gains a .workspaceAccessRevoked case; WirePayload decodes error_code; from() maps 403+code → that case (plain 403 still → .unauthorized). EdgeAPI catch calls WorkspaceScope.handleAccessRevoked() which clears the stale activeOwnerId and posts .workspaceDidChange (ContentView already observes it → resets the local cache + re-pulls under the personal tenant) plus a new .workspaceAccessRevoked notice. The user sees the message via the thrown error's localizedDescription ('You no longer have access to that workspace — switched to your own account') on interactive calls. Added pure EdgeAPIError.from unit tests (403+code → revoked; plain 403 → unauthorized). Verified: deno check + lint clean, 526 edge tests pass. NOTE: a dedicated GLOBAL banner observer for .workspaceAccessRevoked isn't wired (the notification is posted, ready for one) — there's no free-text notice surface in SyncStatusStore; the interactive error-path message covers the AC in practice. iOS not compiled locally (Windows).

userStories.title: Push device-token lifecycle: unregister on sign-out, validate environment, prune dead tokens
userStories.description: As a user who signs out or switches devices, pushes shouldn't keep flowing to a stale token. services/edge-functions/src/routes/notifications.ts:177-243 implements POST /register only — there is no unregister endpoint, the environment field is stored as-is without validating it's 'development'|'production' (a wrong compile-time flag silently kills delivery, ios/GradeThread/Notifications/PushService.swift:126-131), and tokens APNs rejects (410/BadDeviceToken) are never marked inactive or pruned.
acceptanceCriteria: DELETE /api/notifications/register (token in body) removes/deactivates the row; iOS calls it on sign-out and before registering a replacement token
POST /register rejects environment values outside development|production with a 400
The push send path marks tokens inactive when APNs returns Unregistered/BadDeviceToken, and a periodic prune (existing jobs pattern + job lock) deletes long-inactive rows
Account deletion removes the user's push_device_tokens rows (verify the delete-account RPC covers the table; add if missing)

[MEDIUM][Workspace/Security] Mirrors the US-476 pattern (move sensitive writes behind audited service-role routes). DONE 2026-06-10: added audited edge endpoints PATCH /api/workspace/members/:id/role + POST /api/workspace/members/:id/remove (workspace.ts) — caller must be owner/admin (roleAtLeast admin), new role capped via canAssignRole, owner can't be modified/removed (canManageMember rejects owner + above-your-level targets), last-admin self-demotion/self-removal blocked (409), and every change writes admin_audit_log via writeAuditLog. team.tsx updateRole/removeMember now call these endpoints instead of direct workspace_members RLS writes (RLS stays as defense-in-depth). AC3: accept-invite is a direct SPA→PostgREST SECURITY-DEFINER RPC (never transits the edge, so the edge IP limiter can't see it) — added migration 00123 throttling accept_workspace_invitation to 30/min PER AUTHENTICATED USER via the shared increment_rate_limit store (IP isn't available in that RPC context; per-user is the stronger dimension for an auth-required action and is unbypassable since it's in the authoritative RPC). AC4: canManageMember unit tests (non-admin can't manage, owner never manageable, role cap) added to workspace-roles_test. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 526 edge tests pass, frontend tsc + eslint clean. CAVEAT: migration 00123 not applied locally (Docker down → db lane skipped); CI db-migrations.yml validates it on push (it's a verbatim copy of the 00085 function + one increment_rate_limit block). NOTE: HTTP-level integration cases for the new endpoints belong in the env-gated tenant-isolation suite (needs workspace+member fixtures that don't exist yet) — a sensible follow-up; the authorization logic itself is unit-covered. CORRECTION 2026-06-10: migration 00123 (in-RPC accept throttle) was REMOVED — it was ineffective. accept_workspace_invitation runs in one PostgREST transaction; it RAISEs on a bad/expired/email-mismatched token, which rolls back the transaction and UNDOES the increment_rate_limit insert, so failed attempts (the abuse vector) never accumulate — only successful accepts would, which aren't a threat. Persisting a counter across rollback needs autonomous transactions (dblink/pg_background) — disproportionate. AC3 is therefore NOT shipped and is deferred: accepting already requires both a 256-bit token AND an email match, so brute-force is infeasible without it. A correct implementation would route accept through an edge endpoint that rate-limits in its own committed request (real IP), which needs JWT-forwarded RLS calls the codebase deliberately avoids — track as a separate follow-up if enforced accept rate-limiting is wanted. AC1/AC2/AC4 (audited member remove/role endpoints + frontend rewire + canManageMember tests) remain done and effective.

userStories.title: SES bounce/complaint suppression loop
userStories.description: As the platform, I want hard bounces and spam complaints to automatically suppress an address so the autonomous sender never repeatedly mails bad/angry recipients — the safety mechanism that makes hands-off sending viable and protects sender reputation.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds email_suppressions (email unique, reason enum(hard_bounce,complaint,manual,unsubscribe_all), source, created_at, notes).

New public POST /api/email/ses-notifications endpoint receives SES bounce/complaint notifications via SNS (verify the SNS signature; auto-confirm the subscription), classifying hard bounces and complaints and inserting suppressions; transient/soft bounces do NOT suppress.

Every send path (transactional outbox AND marketing) checks email_suppressions first and skips suppressed addresses, recording status='skipped' with reason; a complaint also flips the user's marketing consent off.
A complaint additionally raises an ops alert if the rolling complaint rate exceeds a configurable threshold (settings registry) — over-threshold can auto-pause the newsletter program.
Admin can view suppressions and manually remove a false-positive suppression (audited, super_admin).
Test: a hard-bounce notification suppresses the address and the next campaign skips it.

userStories.title: Autonomous pre-send QA / guardrail gate
userStories.description: As the platform, I want every issue to pass automated quality and safety checks before it can send, so a fully autonomous pipeline never ships a broken, off-brand, or non-compliant email.
acceptanceCriteria: A QA gate runs on each issue before send and blocks on failure: all links resolve (no 404/relative), all images load and have alt text, unsubscribe + preference-center + postal address present, plaintext alternative exists, subject/preheader within length, no spammy-words/ALL-CAPS/excessive punctuation beyond a configurable spam score, and no leftover template/merge-field placeholders.
An AI 'editor' pass (cheap model) checks brand-voice + factual grounding against the issue inputs and flags hallucinated claims; a hard flag blocks send.
Outcome: pass -> issue becomes 'approved' (auto-send) OR 'awaiting_review' when the settings 'require_human_approval' toggle is on; fail -> 'blocked' with reasons + an ops alert.
Results (each check, pass/fail, details) are stored on the issue and shown in the admin console.
A seed-corpus regression test feeds known-bad issues (broken link, missing unsubscribe, hallucinated feature) and asserts each is blocked.
Thresholds live in the settings registry so they're tunable without deploy.

userStories.title: Durable segmented marketing send via outbox
userStories.description: As the platform, I want approved issues delivered to the right segment reliably — through the durable email_deliveries outbox with retry, honoring suppression and consent, idempotently — so sends survive transient failures and never double-mail.
acceptanceCriteria: Sending an approved issue enqueues per-recipient rows that flow through the email_deliveries outbox (category='newsletter') so marketing mail gets the same retry/backoff/dead-letter durability as transactional (closes the US-627 gap where broadcasts had no durable retry).

Recipient resolution = target segment (segments.ts iterateSegmentUsers) UNION confirmed email_subscribers, de-duped by email, MINUS suppressions MINUS users without newsletter consent; each decision recorded as sent/skipped(reason) in campaign_recipients with the UNIQUE(campaign_id,user_id,channel) idempotency guard.

The send is a durable, resumable server-side batch bounded per tick (reuse the bounded-batch pattern from US-407/US-559), honoring the SES warmup rate limiter; a re-run never re-sends an already-sent recipient.
Per-recipient personalization + click-tracking rewriting happen at enqueue/render time.
Each issue links to its campaign_recipients ledger for analytics.
Tenant/consent test: a suppressed or opted-out address is skipped and recorded, never sent.

A test simulates opens across variants and asserts the higher-performing subject is chosen and sent to the holdout.

userStories.title: Trigger & condition engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want a unified trigger engine supporting event-based triggers (first_grade), anchor-relative time triggers (trial_ends_at minus 2 days, signup plus N days), and state/condition predicates (subscription_status, feature-used, inactive N days), so drip steps fire on exactly the right signal. Generalizes the simple daily check sketched in US-929.
acceptanceCriteria: A trigger spec supports three kinds: event (user_events key), time-anchor (anchor field +/- offset; anchors: signup/created_at, trial_ends_at, enrolled_at, last step sent), and state predicate (reuse the segments.ts field/op/value compiler for conditions like subscription_status != active, last_active_at within_days).
An evaluator resolves, for a given user/enrollment, whether a trigger is due now, combining a step's trigger with AND-conditions and skip/branch conditions.
Time anchors handle nulls (no trial_ends_at) and timezones safely; an event trigger can be 'has occurred since enrolled_at'.
The evaluator is pure/testable in isolation with a table of fixtures (trial ends in 2 days -> due; already graded -> skip the nudge; converted -> exit).
Reuses segments.ts predicate compilation rather than a parallel rule language.
No external calls in the evaluator; it operates on a loaded user/enrollment snapshot.

userStories.title: Enrollment & state-machine engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want durable per-user enrollment that advances each user through their drip based on triggers, evaluates branches, and exits on goal/unsub/suppress, idempotently and resumably, so the autonomous sequence runs reliably.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds drip_enrollments (user_id, campaign_id, status enum(active,completed,exited,paused), current_step_key, enrolled_at, next_evaluation_at, context jsonb) with UNIQUE(user_id, campaign_id) so a user enrolls once per campaign.

An enrollment evaluator (lib/drip-engine.ts) loads due enrollments, evaluates the current/eligible steps via the trigger engine, sends the due step through the coordinator+outbox, advances current_step_key (honoring branches/skips), and exits on goal/unsub/suppress/end.

Enrollment is created when a user matches a campaign's entry trigger (e.g. signup -> trial_conversion); evaluation is idempotent (a step is sent at most once per enrollment, guarded by a sent-steps ledger).
Processing is a bounded, resumable server-side batch (reuse US-407/US-559 pattern) safe to re-run; a crash mid-batch never double-sends.
Exit reasons are recorded (converted/unsubscribed/suppressed/completed) for analytics.
Tests: a trialist who converts on day 8 exits and receives no further drip steps; a dormant trialist gets the inactivity branch.

userStories.title: Durable per-step send with personalization & tracking
userStories.description: As the platform, I want each drip step delivered through the durable outbox with consent, suppression, personalization, and open/click tracking, so drip emails are as reliable and measurable as the newsletter.
acceptanceCriteria: Drip step sends route through the US-925 durable email_deliveries outbox (category='drip:<campaign>:<step>') with retry/backoff/dead-letter, the US-924 QA gate, and the US-913 open/click tracking rewriter.
Per-recipient personalization (US-921) fills dynamic blocks (their grades/listings/sales this trial, trial days left, what they haven't tried) at render time.
Every send is checked against consent (US-911 newsletter/marketing), suppression (US-914), and the frequency coordinator before dispatch; skips are recorded with reason.
Sends are idempotent per (enrollment, step) and recorded to campaign_recipients (or a drip equivalent) for analytics + A/B variant tracking.
Plaintext alternative + CAN-SPAM footer + one-click unsubscribe present on every drip email.
A test asserts a suppressed/opted-out trialist is skipped (recorded), not sent.
